Note: For sub-case A, companies report at least one of two Benchmarks with the correspondent complexity. Note: For sub-case B, companies report Benchmark 2 and its correspondent complexity. Note: If companies report a comparison between Sub-Case A and Sub-Case B, the report must consider at least benchmark 2 with the correspondent complexity either sub-case A and/or sub-case B. Case 2: The AI model is trained based on training dataset from one Scenario #A/Configuration #A, and then the AI model performs inference/test on a different dataset than Scenario #A/Configuration #A, e.g., Scenario #B/Configuration #B, Scenario #A/Configuration #B. Case 3: The AI model is trained based on training dataset constructed by mixing datasets from multiple scenarios/configurations including Scenario #A/Configuration #A and a different dataset than Scenario #A/Configuration #A, e.g., Scenario #B/Configuration #B, Scenario #A/Configuration #B, and then the AI model performs inference/test on a dataset from a single Scenario/Configuration from the multiple scenarios/configurations, e.g., Scenario #A/Configuration #A, Scenario #B/Configuration #B, Scenario #A/Configuration #B. | RAN1#125 | 10.2.1 | Agreement | Draft LS in R1-2605068 is endorsed in principle with following updates. Final LS in R1-2605069 is endorsed.<br>---<br>1	Overall description<br>RAN1 discussed coverage improvements through low PAPR enhancements for uplink DFT-s-OFDM waveform for 6GR.<br>RAN1#125 in May 2026 in Dalian reached an agreement that Frequency Domain Spectrum Shaping (FDSS) with transparent filtering is beneficial at least for π/2-BPSK. The exact wording of the RAN1 agreement is copied below:<br>\| Agreement: FDSS with transparent filtering is beneficial to be supported for π/2-BPSK from RAN1 perspective FFS: QPSK, 16QAM Draft LS to RAN4 FFS: contents e.g., “the exact filter requirements are up to RAN4 discussions.” \|<br>RAN1 has also been studying other PAPR enhancement techniques, with observations made in RA1#125.<br>2	Actions<br>To RAN4<br>ACTION: 	RAN1 respectfully asks RAN4 to take the RAN1 agreement on FDSS with transparent filtering into account in their work on 6GR.<br>3	Dates of next TSG RAN meetings<br>RAN WG#126		24th – 28th August, 2026	Maastricht, Netherlands<br>RAN WG#126bis	12th – 16th October, 2026	Jeju, Korea<br>--- | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2605068](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2605068.zip) |

| RAN1#125 | 10.2.1 | Agreement | Following RAN1 report contents on waveform for communication to RAN are endorsed.<br>Waveform for communication<br>\| What RAN1 has discussed/observed/ agreed \| RAN1 agreed to support CP-OFDM for DL and CP-OFDM/DFT-s-OFDM for UL as defined in 5G NR for 6GR. RAN1 has prioritized the studies on “UL coverage improvement through low UL PAPR enhancement for DFT-s-OFDM” and “multi-rank UL-MIMO for DFT-s-OFDM”. RAN1 agreed to support maximum rank = 2 for multi-rank UL-MIMO for DFT-s-OFDM. RAN1 agreed to support semi-static and dynamic UL waveform switching RAN1 agreed for low UL PAPR enhancement for DFT-s-OFDM that for pi/2 BPSK, Frequency Domain Spectrum Shaping (FDSS) with transparent filtering is beneficial to be supported, and liaised RAN4 accordingly. RAN1 has captured interim observations on other PAPR enhancement techniques for UL DFT-s-OFDM RAN1 noted the study on other waveforms, and RAN1 concluded that further discussion is not planned in waveform agenda item in RAN1 unless tasked by RAN. \|<br>\| What RAN1 plans to continue studying after June \| On low UL PAPR enhancement for DFT-s-OFDM: Further work after June 2026 is required in order to draw definite conclusions on the benefits and potential RAN1 spec impacts of spectral extension/truncation techniques with transparent/non-transparent filtering, the benefits and potential RAN1 spec impacts of non-transparent filtering with no spectral extension/truncation techniques. \|<br>\| What RAN1 plans not to pursue after June \| RAN1 plans not to pursue the study on other waveforms than CP-OFDM for DL and CP-OFDM/DFT-s-OFDM for UL in waveform agenda item in RAN1 unless tasked by RAN. \|<br>\| What RAN1 requests RAN guidance/ decision if any \|  \| | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603728](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603728.zip) |

| RAN1#125 | 10.3.1 | Conclusion | Report the following for interim RAN1 report on Coding check point.<br>\| What RAN1 has discussed/observed/agreed \| RAN1 agreed for 6G channel coding, LDPC is used for data (including SIBs) and Polar code is used for L1 control information (larger than 11 bits, including PBCH). RAN1 agreed for 6G data channel coding: 1) working assumption is that reuse of NR LDPC design is supported for data rate within NR range; 2) study LDPC extension for data rate beyond NR range. In addition, RAN1 studied and identified the structure and parameters of potential LDPC extension. The evaluation results of LDPC code extension beyond NR range have been captured in R1-2605123. RAN1 agreed on the framework of application condition of potential LDPC extension, if introduced. RAN1 agreed for 6G control channel coding: 1) RAN1 working assumption is that for control information within NR range (larger than 11 bits), reuse of NR Polar code design is supported. RAN1 concluded there is no consensus on motivation(s) for potential extension/enhancement for Polar code design for payload size within NR range (larger than 11bits). 2) study Polar code extension for payload size beyond NR range based on the evaluation assumptions in RAN1#124. In addition, RAN1 agreed to study more than 2 segments for Polar code with UCI payload size larger than 1706 bits. RAN1 agreed for 6G small UCI with 3~11 bits: 1) RAN1 agreed to at least consider 5G RM code for small UCI with payload size of 3~11 bits, identify the justifiable drawback of 5G RM code, if exists, study potential solution(s). \|<br>\| What RAN1 plans to continue studying after June \| RAN1 plans to continue to study Polar code extension for payload size beyond NR range (larger than 11bits). RAN1 plans to continue to identify the justifiable drawbacks of 5G RM code, if exists, study potential solution(s). \|<br>\| What RAN1 plans not to pursue after June \| RAN1 plans not to pursue Polar code extension for payload size within NR range (larger than 11bits) after June. \|<br>\| What RAN1 requests RAN guidance/decision if any \| RAN1 needs RAN guidance on if and how to proceed on the remaining study for LDPC code extension. \| | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2605018](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2605018.zip)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Channel coding]` |

| RAN1#126bis | 10.3.2 | Agreement | For performance study to allow a single spectrum efficiency point (subject to quantization error) to be supported by multiple  pairs, both fixed SE simulations and simulations with link adaptation are needed.<br>- The performance study is to identify if the preferred  pair changes with respect to channel profile, rank, spatial-layer imbalance, receiver type, Doppler, EVM, UL power back-off, and LDPC code<br>  - FFS: Other factors that may affect the preferred  pair choice<br>- For channels to be evaluated<br>  - The set of fading channels include: CDL-A 100ns, CDL-B 30ns, CDL-C 300ns, CDL-D 30ns<br>    - Other fading channel can be included in the set, per company report<br>  - The set of MIMO schemes include: SIMO 1x4 (UL), MIMO 4x4 (DL), MIMO 2x4 (UL), MIMO32x4 (DL), MIMO2x32 (UL)<br>    - Other MIMO schemes can be included in the set, per company report<br>- Precoder assumption: Closed loop precoder. Open loop precoder for high Doppler channels (at least 200Hz).<br>- CW to layer mapping: NR CW to layer mapping as baseline.<br>  - Other CW to layer mapping can be reported<br>- LDPC: NR BG1/BG2 as baseline<br>  - BG3 results can be reported.<br>- For UL, both DFTs and CP-OFDM waveform can be evaluated<br>  - Other waveform can be reported<br>- For fixed SE simulations<br>  - The SE points of current NR are used as starting point of the evaluation. #### 10.4.1 Operation in idle mode

| RAN1#126 | 10.4.1 | Agreement | For further study of initial access for idle mode multi-carrier operation, consider at least the following potential use cases:<br>  - UC-1: UL coverage enhancement / DL-UL coverage imbalance<br>  - UC-2: RACH capacity / offloading / load balancing<br>  - UC-3: Network energy saving / common-signaling reduction<br>  - Other use cases are not precluded.<br>  - For each identified use case, study whether and under which conditions multiple-carrier operation in idle mode provides additional benefit over existing mechanisms. | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-MC-Operation in idle mode]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.4.1 | Agreement | For study of multiple carriers where for initial access a UE can utilize resources for UL (Msg1, etc) or for both UL (Msg1, etc.) and DL (Msg2, etc.) in one carrier other than the carrier where the UE obtains the system information providing configuration for those resources, consider the following potential scenarios for the set of candidate physical carriers for which resources are provided for initial access:<br>  - S1: 1 DL physical carrier + N UL physical carriers, where N > 1<br>  - S2: M DL physical carriers + 1 UL physical carrier, where M > 1<br>  - S3: M DL physical carriers + N UL physical carriers, where M > 1 and N > 1<br>Note 1: The carrier where the UE obtains the system information and other candidate physical carrier(s) are counted above.<br>Note 2: For a given UE and a given initial access procedure, UE may use only a subset of the candidate physical carrier.<br>Note 3: The inclusion of a scenario for study does not imply agreement to support it. The need and applicable use cases/deployment scenarios for each scenario are subject to further study. | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-MC-Operation in idle mode]` |

There is no implication that RAN4 should use the same assumption.<br>2. | RAN1#124bis | 10.5.1.2 | Agreement | Adopt the following definition for miss detection probability and false alarm probability for RAN1 study (not intended for 6GR requirements)<br>- Note: Definition of evaluation metrics are for the purpose of alignment of definition among companies. Companies are encouraged to provide information on evaluation metrics reported and the implication and importance of the evaluation metric in the contributions with evaluations.<br>- Miss detection probability<br>  - Total probability of following events (for a preamble transmission):<br>    - Not detecting the preamble for a RO that was sent among the target preambles of the detecting BS<br>    - Correct preamble detection but with the wrong timing estimation<br>      - For correct preamble detection, the (residual) timing estimation error should be less than CP/2 of data symbol, e.g., SCS = 30kHz, CP/2 = 1.2 us<br>- False alarm probability<br>  - Probability of detecting any target preamble for a RO when no transmission has occurred (only noise)<br>Adopt the following definition for metrics for evaluations for RAN1 study (not intended for 6GR requirements)<br>- Note: Not all metrics may be applicable for all evaluation scenarios, and it is up to companies to provide appropriate metric(s) for information. The definitions are for the purpose of alignment of definition among companies. Companies are encouraged to provide information on evaluation metrics reported and the implication and importance of the evaluation metric in the contributions with evaluations.<br>- Miss detection probability considering frequency estimation<br>  - Total probability of following events (for a preamble transmission):<br>    - Not detecting the preamble for a RO that was sent among the target preambles of the detecting BS<br>    - Correct preamble detection but with the wrong timing estimation and/or frequency estimation<br>      - For correct preamble detection,<br>        - the (residual) timing estimation error should be less than CP/2 of data symbol, e.g., SCS = 30kHz, CP/2 = 1.2 us, and<br>        - the (residual) frequency estimation error of PRACH detection should be less than some target value. Target value to be reported by company.<br>- Type 1 false detection probability (intra-cell)<br>  - Probability of detecting different preamble(s) for a RO than the one that was sent among the target preambles of the detecting BS.<br>- Type 1 false detection rate (intra-cell)<br>  - A = number of preamble(s) for a RO detected other than the one that was sent among the target preambles of the detecting BS<br>  - B = Sum of A for all ROs that contain preamble transmission<br>  - C = Total number of preamble transmission across all ROs<br>  - Type 1 false detection rate = B divided by C<br>- Type 2 false detection probability (inter-cell)<br>  - Probability of detecting any target preamble for a RO when no transmission has occurred in the cell of detecting BS and transmission has occurred in another cell<br>- Mixed false detection probability<br>  - Probability of detecting multiple preambles (two or more) of which one of the detected preamble is correctly detected (multiple preamble detection for the detecting BS) for a RO when only one preamble among the target preambles of the detection BS was sent. | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-PRACH]` |
| RAN1#124bis | 10.5.1.2 | Agreement | - Study base sequences and preamble sequence generation/construction methods for 6GR PRACH taking into account one or more of the following aspects:<br>  - detection performance (possibly including TA estimation performance, handling of frequency offset, miss-detection, false alarm, false detection, auto-correlation/cross correlation properties, etc)<br>  - detection complexity for BS<br>  - implementation complexity for UE<br>  - Cubic metric/PAPR<br>  - supported sequence lengths & associated SCS of a sequence<br>  - [Preambles per random access occasion (RO) ]<br>  - Inter-cell interference<br>  - Coexistence with 5G NR PRACH sequences<br>  - Note 1: Benchmark various performance metric(s) and considerations against 5G NR PRACH design as baseline<br>  - Note 2: base sequences for 5G NR PRACH are ZC sequence, and preamble sequence generation is done via (time domain) cyclic shift of a ZC root sequence (base sequence) to create a specific preamble sequence.<br>  - Note 3: companies are encouraged to provide the following information:<br>    - detailed information for the sequence generation and construction of a preamble for PRACH<br>    - correlation properties (compared to NR PRACH sequences, including correlation with NR PRACH sequences)<br>    - Cubic metric/PAPR (at least compared to NR PRACH sequences)<br>    - Applicable scenarios | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-PRACH]` |

| RAN1#126 | 10.5.1.2 | Agreement | For the study of preamble format reduction, below template is adopted for companies to provide set of preamble design targets that provide enablement of 6GR use cases and deployment scenarios. Please provide minimal set of preamble design targets that companies believe is the best representation for 6GR, including information on how the representative preamble design targets for 6GR is selected.<br>- A row represented Preamble design targets are represented by {Carrier Frequency, Delay (Max RTT + Delay Spread), Doppler Shift} tuple.<br>\| Identifier (company + Index) \| Carrier Frequency \| Delay (Max RTT + Delay Spread) \| Doppler Shift \| Notes (any information to additional share, e.g., sequence length, occupied BW, SCS, number of sequence repetition, preamble duration, frame structure restrictions, information on derivation, motivation, etc) \|<br>\|  \|  \|  \|  \|  \|<br>\|  \|  \|  \|  \|  \|<br>\|  \|  \|  \|  \|  \|<br>\|  \|  \|  \|  \|  \| | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-PRACH]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.5.1.2 | Conclusion | To report the following details for PRACH evaluations:<br>- Receiver algorithm details, including:<br>  - Detection threshold strategy:<br>    - threshold configured to address false alarm only (impacting miss detection)<br>      - Example 1) Threshold is determined based on noise variance<br>    - threshold configured to address false alarm (impacting miss detection) and false detection probability jointly<br>      - Example 2) Threshold is determined based on noise variance, inter-sequence interference + noise estimated from measurements outside the window of the detected peak<br>        - Detection metric is normalized by interference+noise estimate, where the estimate is derived (e.g., maximum or median of the detection metric) from the detection metric outside the window around the detected peak within the NCS duration of the preamble. The detection peak window can be +/- estimated/approximated channel delay.<br>      - Example 3) Threshold is determined based on noise variance, sequence interference estimated from measurement of total receive signal power of a RO<br>  - In case of ZC sequence detection with Restricted Set A and B, details of detection algorithm to handle the detection sidelobes.<br>- For False alarm statistics, which option used for false alarm (and determination of detection threshold)<br>  - Option 1) if BS performs detection on a RO, the false alarm event happens for a preamble sequence detection, and a false alarm event is counted for the preamble sequence (false alarm event may happen multiple times within a RO for across the multiple preamble sequences). In this case, the denominator used to compute false alarm probability is the number of preambles to be detected (per RO).<br>  - Option 2) if BS performs detection on a RO, the false alarm event happens for any preamble sequence detection, and the a single false alarm event counted for a RO. In this case, denominator used to compute false alarm probability is 1 (per RO).<br>- Relative Tx power assumption of UEs (and any pathloss measurement and RF impairment modeling, if used)<br>- User distribution per RO, for example<br>  - Same number of users transmitting PRACH preamble in each RO<br>  - Varying number of users transmitting PRACH preamble in each RO (may be based on traffic characteristics)<br>- Preamble sequence selection<br>  - For example, NR ZC provides information on number of root sequences, number of cyclic shifts, and Ncs value among the 64 preamble set used for evaluation. | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-PRACH]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.5.1.2 | Agreement | For study of whether the maximum number of preambles per RO is increased beyond 64, take into account at least:<br>- the justification and use case for the capacity increase (e.g., load model, access rate per cell, target collision probability, availability of ROs in time/frequency);<br>- the available root-sequence pool and the resulting inter-cell reusing for the assumed sequence length; and<br>  - Note: Preamble sequence, format, as well as availability of ROs in time/frequency are taken into account when calculating available sequence pool and reuse.<br>- the resulting Miss detection, Type-1 (intra-cell), and Type-2 (inter-cell) false-detection performance under PRACH transmission load in the network.<br>  - Companies are asked to provide information on detection algorithm and detection metric thresholds (and adaptation strategies, if any) used for evaluations.<br>- associated transmitter/receiver complexity, and random access latency | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-PRACH]` |
| RAN1#126bis | 10.5.1.2 | Agreement | In addition to uniform SSB-to-RO mapping, study non-uniform SSB-to-RO mapping, and other reference signal-to-RO mapping (if necessary).<br>Chair note: Msg 3 payload size and associated coverage study evaluations are expected to be handled under 10.5.1.1 | [Chair notes RAN1#126bis_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126bis_eom1.docx)<br>`[126bis-R20-6GR-PRACH]` |

| RAN1#126bis | 10.5.1.2 | Agreement | For RAN2 LS reply on random access in 6G [R1-2605183/R2-2604385]:<br>- RAN1 has not yet studied the design of 2-step RA for 6GR and the answers to Q1 and Q2 are based on 5G NR 2-step design which may or may not be applicable for 6GR. The following is agreements regarding RA procedure in RAN1:<br>\| Agreement Adopt 4-step RACH as the baseline procedure for 6GR. Study 2-step RACH, RACH-less/contention-based-PUSCH access for UEs with adequate uplink timing alignment, dedicated RACH (1-step) as additional procedure(s). Study for 2-step RACH to include aspects asked by RAN2 in LS R1-2605183/R2-2604385 Justifications of the potential additional procedure(s) \|<br>- Question 1 (whether it is possible to support 2-step and 4-step RA when they are both configured with the same preamble and RACH occasion):<br>  - RAN1 has not yet studied 2-step RA design and not yet assessed feasibility for 6GR. RAN1 has identified at least the following aspects based on 5G NR 2-step Preamble and MsgA:<br>    - The gNB attempts PUSCH reception for a detected preamble and falls back to 4-step RA when the PUSCH is not successfully received, which increases the number of blind PUSCH detections at the gNB.<br>    - If 4-step RA is configured together with 2-step RA, the response for a 4-step RA UE may need to be delayed until after the PUSCH occasion, which may increase 4-step RA latency and/or reduce the resources available for RAR transmission within the response window.<br>    - Distinguishing which procedure a UE has initiated is not deterministic from the preamble alone, which has implications on RAR/fallback handling.<br>- Question 2 (for 2-step RA, whether it is necessary to have correspondence between PRACH and PUSCH transmissions in MsgA, and if so how to establish it):<br>  - From RAN1 perspective, correspondence is necessary, at least for the following functions based on 5G NR 2-step Preamble and MsgA:<br>    - determination of the PUSCH resource associated with a detected preamble,<br>    - PUSCH scrambling and multiplexing of UEs sharing an RO,<br>    - timing-advance handling, and identification of the UE in the fallback RAR.<br>  - Note that RAN1 has not made any agreements on physical signals/channels of 2-step RA for 6GR and applicability of correspondence is currently undetermined.<br>- Note: RAN1 will continue the study of the above aspects and will inform RAN2 if the answers need to be updated. | [Chair notes RAN1#126bis_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126bis_eom1.docx)<br>`[126bis-R20-6GR-PRACH]` |

| RAN1#126 | 10.5.2.1 | Agreement | Companies are encouraged to provide the analysis for comparison of MU-MIMO schemes (based on orthogonal and/or non-orthogonal DMRS) and single-layer, single-port, single-user PDCCH considering<br>  - The necessity to introduce orthogonal DMRS for 6GR PDCCH<br>  - At least the following two cases:<br>    - Case1: double resources for two paired MU-MIMO UEs than for a single user and the same total power are assumed from NW point of view<br>    - Case 2: the same resources for single user and two paired MU-MIMO users and the same total power are assumed from NW point of view<br>  - Performance based on link level and/or system level evaluations (e.g., BLER, spectrum efficiency)<br>  - Used models and criteria on the user pairing for MU-MIMO based on orthogonal multi-port DMRS and/or non-orthogonal single-port DMRS<br>  - Assumptions on the UE receiver<br>  - Assumptions on UE specific precoding<br>  - Impacts on UE complexity<br>  - Assumed channel model (at least CDL channel model for link level evaluations)<br>  - Assumed DCI size<br>Note: The discussion of the utilization of orthogonal DMRS ports for other purposes (e.g. intercell-interference mitigation) than MU-MIMO is not precluded. | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2606614](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2606614.zip)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-Transmission scheme for DL control channel]` |

| RAN1#126bis | 10.5.2.1 | Agreement | For the further study of the CCE-to-REG mapping for overlapping CORESETs (e.g., wideband and narrowband 6GR CORESETs, and NR and 6GR CORESETs for MRSS), consider the following as starting point:<br>- Option 1: Only one CCE-to-REG mapping is applied for a 6GR CORESET, PDCCH candidates are mapped only to a single CORESET, independently if CORESETs partially overlap, in a way transparent for the UE.<br>- Further discuss necessity and feasibility of the following options including UE transparency aspects .<br>  - Option 2: Only one CCE-to-REG mapping is applied for a 6GR CORESET, but PDCCH candidate can use CCEs of more than one of the non-overlapping CORESETs aggregated in time and/or frequency<br>    - FFS whether the same CCE-to-REG mapping scheme should be used for all aggregated CORESETs or not.<br>    - FFS the maximum number of aggregated CORESETs.<br>    - FFS whether CORESETs should be adjacent to each other in time/frequency or not.<br>  - Option 3: Same CCE-to-REG mapping scheme (interleaved or non-interleaved) is independently applied to multiple sets of resources within 6GR CORESET<br>    - The sets do not overlap in both time and frequency<br>      - FFS how to define time-frequency resources per set<br>    - Option 3a: The sets are multiplexed in frequency<br>    - Option 3b: The sets are multiplexed in time<br>    - FFS whether a PDCCH candidate can use CCEs of more than one sets of resources.<br>    - FFS: whether the sets of resources are multiplexed in both time and frequency<br>    - FFS: the maximum number of sets in a 6G CORESET | [Chair notes RAN1#126bis_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126bis_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2608526](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Docs/R1-2608526.zip)<br>`[126bis-R20-6GR-Transmission scheme for DL control channel]` |

| RAN1#124bis | 10.5.2.2 | Agreement | - Study codeword-to-layer mapping for PDSCH:<br>  - Consider the following aspects<br>    - The number of codewords for each rank<br>    - The maximum number of codewords<br>    - The maximum rank per codeword<br>    - The modulation order per layer(s)<br>  - Including identifying and evaluating important aspects affecting performance and complexity that are impacted by codeword-to-layer mapping<br>  - NR spatial first, frequency second, time third mapping as baseline for evaluation<br>  - NR codeword-to-layer mapping as baseline for evaluation<br>- Further study whether/how to map one or more transport block(s) to time/frequency resources and its impact on codeword-to-layer mapping<br>- Further study aspects related to modulation order and code rate and its impact on codeword-to-layer mapping | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-Transmission scheme for DL shared channel]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.2.2 | Agreement | - Support DMRS-based PDSCH transmission with one DMRS port per layer, where the layers and DMRS ports are precoded using the same precoders<br>  - Note: Whether/how to additionally support multiple DMRS ports per layer and/or DMRS-free PDSCH transmission is a separate discussion | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Transmission scheme for DL shared channel]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.2.2 | Agreement | - Support both SU-MIMO and MU-MIMO for PDSCH. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Transmission scheme for DL shared channel]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.2.2 | Agreement | - For DMRS based on TD-OCC-X for a single-slot based PDSCH, the TD-OCC-X is applied to X consecutive symbols for DMRS<br>  - Consider the same spacing between every X DMRS symbols<br>    - Study how to identify the spacing between every X DMRS symbols<br>    - FFS: whether there is any exception<br>  - The number of DMRS symbols in a slot is L*X, and study the candidate value of L as follows<br>    - For X = 1, L = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}<br>    - For X = 2, L = {1, 2, 3}<br>    - For X = 4, L = {1}<br>    - If multiple candidate values of L are supported, study how to determine the value of L<br>    - Note: Above does not mean X = {1, 2, 4} are all supported<br>  - Study at least the following options for the time-domain location of the first DMRS symbol<br>    - Option 1: The first DMRS symbol is fixed as the first symbol allocated for the PDSCH<br>    - Option 2: The candidate DMRS symbol(s) are fixed in a slot and the actual first DMRS symbol is the first candidate DMRS symbol within the TDRA for the PDSCH<br>    - Option 3: The first DMRS symbol is indicated by the network relative to the first symbol of the PDSCH | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Transmission scheme for DL shared channel]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.2.2 | Agreement | - For low overhead DMRS with AI/ML receiver for PDSCH reception, reuse the LLS EVM for PDSCH and RS agreed in RAN1 #124b<br>  - Support the following additional EVM for generalization/scalability of the AI/ML models across one or multiple of the followings<br>    - Various channel models, e.g., various CDL models<br>    - Various delay spread<br>    - Various Doppler spread<br>    - Various SINR<br>    - Various carrier frequencies<br>    - Various UE speed<br>    - Various UE antenna operations, e.g., UE selected antennas for DL reception, number of UE antennas, etc.<br>    - Various aNB antenna configurations, e.g., antenna spacing, TXRU mapping, antenna layout, etc.<br>    - Various downlink transmission operations, e.g., TDRA, FDRA, MCS, DMRS antenna port(s), PRG size, precoders, etc.<br>    - Various number of MIMO layers<br>  - Companies shall report the number of model parameters, AI/ML receiver related aspects (including at least model input, model output, and label) for the AI/ML model<br>    - Companies shall report the number of FLOPs, FLOPs per RB/slot/layer, together with the corresponding inference configuration (e.g., number of Rx antennas, number of subcarriers, number of symbols and number of layers for PDSCH)<br>    - Companies can optionally report whether/how the labelling error is modelled<br>  - The following model generalization aspects defined in TR38.843 can be further considered<br>    - Case 1: The AI model is trained based on training dataset from one Scenario #A/Configuration #A, and then the AI model performs inference/test on a dataset from the same Scenario #A/Configuration #A.<br>    - Case 2: The AI model is trained based on training dataset from one Scenario #A/Configuration #A, and then the AI model performs inference/test on a different dataset than Scenario #A/Configuration #A, e.g., Scenario #B/Configuration #B, Scenario #A/Configuration #B.<br>    - Case 3: The AI model is trained based on training dataset constructed by mixing datasets from multiple scenarios/configurations including Scenario #A/Configuration #A and a different dataset than Scenario #A/Configuration #A, e.g., Scenario #B/Configuration #B, Scenario #A/Configuration #B, and then the AI model performs inference/test on a dataset from a single Scenario/Configuration from the multiple scenarios/configurations, e.g., Scenario #A/Configuration #A, Scenario #B/Configuration #B, Scenario #A/Configuration #B. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Transmission scheme for DL shared channel]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.2.2 | Agreement | - Study multi-TRP transmission for PDSCH(s), considering, at least, the following aspects:<br>  - Whether/how to support single PDSCH from a single TRP and/or from multiple TRPs, and/or multiple PDSCHs from multiple TRPs<br>  - Strive to minimize the number of multi-TRP transmission schemes<br>    - E.g., avoid multiple schemes targeting the same scenario<br>  - Whether/how to design common framework for both single-TRP and multi-TRP transmission<br>  - Study of multi-TRP transmission to include identifying deployment conditions and operating regimes where multi-TRP transmission provides performance/energy saving benefits relative to single-TRP transmission<br>    - E.g., high-speed train (HST) scenario | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Transmission scheme for DL shared channel]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.2.2 | Agreement | - For frequency interleaving of PDSCH:<br>  - Support non-interleaved frequency mapping<br>  - Study interleaved frequency mapping, considering, at least, the following aspects:<br>    - Applicability to one or both of RIV-based and RBG-based mapping<br>    - Mapping granularity<br>    - Number of scheduled RBs<br>    - Whether the interleaving is within one of the following:<br>      - Subset or all of scheduled/allocated RB(s)<br>      - Configured/predefined interleaving bandwidth(s)<br>      - Subset or all of scheduled/allocated RB(s) within a configured/predefined interleaving bandwidth(s)<br>      - FFS: Definition of interleaving bandwidth(s)<br>      - FFS: Whether configured/predefined interleaving bandwidth(s) is independent of scheduled/allocated RB(s)<br>    - Impact on performance compared to non-interleaved frequency mapping and compared to NR interleaved frequency mapping<br>    - Impact on latency<br>    - Impact on multiplexing/scheduling<br>    - Impact on transmitter/receiver complexity | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Transmission scheme for DL shared channel]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.2.2 | Agreement | - For precoding granularity of PDSCH on a single physical carrier:<br>  - Support PRB bundling, where UE assumes that precoding granularity is N consecutive PRBs in the frequency domain, and UE may assume the same precoding is applied within the precoding granularity<br>    - Note: How precoding is performed within the precoding granularity is up to aNB implementation<br>  - Further study which PRB bundling sizes, i.e., N, should be supported, considering, at least, support for wider bandwidth (more than 275 RBs), DMRS design, and UE-specific/common PDSCH transmission<br>    - PRB bundling sizes supported in NR as starting point for study<br>  - Further study potential impact (if any) of 2 RF chains at the UE for 400 MHz CBW<br>  - Further study whether PRB bundling size is layer-common or layer-specific<br>  - Note: Decision to study PRB bundling for the case of scheduling across multiple physical carriers is subject to agreements in other agenda items<br>  - FFS: Per subcarrier/PRB precoding granularity | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Transmission scheme for DL shared channel]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.2.2 | Agreement | - For FDRA for PDSCH on a single physical carrier:<br>  - For RBG-based mapping:<br>    - Support nominal RBG size P larger than 16 RBs<br>    - Further study specific values for nominal RBG size<br>    - Further study whether nominal RBG size is configurable | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Transmission scheme for DL shared channel]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.2.2 | Agreement | - For FDRA for PDSCH on a single physical carrier:<br>  - For RIV-based mapping:<br>    - Minimum granularity is 1 RB<br>    - Further study maximum granularity<br>    - Further study whether granularity is configurable | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Transmission scheme for DL shared channel]` |

| RAN1#126 | 10.5.2.3 | Agreement | The following is endorsed  as Draft an LS to RAN4 regarding the 6GR the RF coherence requirements.<br>1 Overall description:<br>RAN1 are studying UL MIMO codebooks for 6G and have reached the following agreements:<br>\| Agreement: For codebook based PUSCH transmission for 6GR, study fixed codebook for full-coherent precoder type considering the following options and aspects: Option 1. Reuse NR UL codebook Option 2. Grassmannian codebook Option 3. Per-element phase/amplitude quantization targeting SVD precoder approximation Option 4. DFT based precoder Other option(s) are not precluded. Consider different antenna architectures and different waveforms Whether/how to separately or commonly design 2TX/3TX/4TX/8TX codebook Whether to keep constant modulus property Whether/how to consider UE PA (power amplifier) constraint Whether/how to define single-layer precoder only, and indicating a combination of precoder(s) Consider different codebook size and precoder indication overhead Whether/how to separately or commonly design codebook for CP-OFDM and DFT-S-OFDM. Note: Partial/non-coherent precoder type are separately discussed. Note: Per-layer power control is separately discussed. Agreement: For evaluation on coherent UL MIMO based PUSCH transmission for 6GR, at least the RF coherence requirements for coherent UL MIMO defined in TS38.101-1/2 are used as baseline Companies to report Other additional RF coherence requirements can be reported by companies (optional) TX coherency error model \|<br>RAN1 are currently using the coherent UL MIMO requirements in TS38.101-1/2 as baselines for evaluations including coherence imperfections. RAN1 would like to know if the /phase errors in these requirements  for 6G, especially for devices that support more than two port UL MIMO transmission.<br>RAN1 have not so far agreed to models of coherence imperfections for codebook evaluations, and so such models are determined by each company. Therefore, while RAN1 can continue investigations, RAN1 would welcome suggestions on /phase error modeling for 6G UEs so that these may be used to refine RAN1’s evaluations.<br>2	Actions<br>To RAN4<br>ACTION: 	RAN1 respectfully asks RAN4 if the /phase errors in current coherent UL MIMO requirements in TS38.101-1/2  for 6G, especially for devices that support more than two port UL MIMO transmission. While RAN1 can continue investigations, RAN1 would also welcome suggestions on /phase error modeling for UL MIMO.<br>The corresponding final LS in R1-2606899 is endorsed. | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2605832](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2605832.zip)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-Transmission scheme for UL channels]` |

| RAN1#126 | 10.5.2.3 | Agreement | For codebook based PUSCH transmission for 6GR, study configurable codebook considering the following options and aspects:<br>- Option 1. Downloadable codebook<br>  - NW determines a set of precoder(s)/matrices.<br>  - From NW, UE is configured with a set of precoder(s)/matrices.<br>  - After NW acquires UL CSI, an UL precoder within the set of precoder(s) is indicated by NW to UE.<br>- Option 2. Uploadable codebook<br>  - UE determines a set of precoder(s) and reports to NW.<br>  - From NW, UE is configured with a set of precoder(s).<br>  - After NW acquires UL CSI, an UL precoder within the set of precoder(s) is indicated by NW to UE.<br>- Whether to consider constant modulus property<br>- Whether/how to indicate/obtain UE’s relevant information<br>- How to construct hybrid approach between fixed codebook and configurable codebook<br>- Memory burden / implementation complexity for UE/NW side<br>- Applicable scenario/use case (e.g., applicable number of antenna ports)<br>- How to consider PAPR increase and UE power constraint | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2605832](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2605832.zip)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-Transmission scheme for UL channels]` |

| RAN1#126bis | 10.5.2.3 | Agreement | For the study of AI based receiver for PUSCH DMRS overhead reduction, the following template is used as a starting point to collect companies’ results via LLS:<br>Note: the following template is an update from the agreed LLS table for AI based receiver for PUSCH DMRS overhead reduction. The update part is shown in red text.<br>\| Parameters \| Value \|<br>\| #0 sub-case \| Reported by company. \|<br>\| #1 Receiver assumptions \| Reported up to company, for example, Details on Receiver options (in R1-2509598) Option 1: AI-based denoise on DMRS REs only Option 2: AI-based channel estimation for data REs (with or without denoise on DMRS REs) Option 3: AI based channel prediction for target REs Option 4: AI-based joint {channel estimation + equalization + demodulation/LLR calculation} Option 5: AI-based {channel estimation} + AI-based {equalization + demodulation/LLR calculation} Additional Receiver options Option 6: Channel estimation + equalization + AI-based {demodulation/LLR calculation} Option 7: AI-based {Channel estimation} + equalization + AI-based {demodulation/LLR calculation} Other receiver options are not precluded Note: Receiver type (such as AI/non-AI) including the above Options in aNB will not be specified. \|<br>\| #2 Model input \| Reported by company, including input content and input dimension \|<br>\| #3 Model output \| Reported by company, including output content and output dimension \|<br>\| #4 Label \| If applicable, reported by company, including label acquisition method and label error (e.g., zero for ideal label, or non-zero for realistic label) (Labelling error model can be reported optionally) (Cost function can be reported optionally) \|<br>\| #5 Training type \| Offline \|<br>\| #6 Number of MIMO layers \| Reported by company \|<br>\| #7 Number of FLOPs (for receiver block replaced by AIML model) \| Reported by company Company also reports Inference related parameters for PUSCH (e.g., number of RBs, symbols) (“Number of FLOPs per RB/slot/layer” or “Number of FLOPs per RB/slot/layer/Rx Antenna” can be reported optionally) \|<br>\| #7-1 Number of FLOPs (for receiver block not replaced by AIML model) \| Number of FLOPs of non-AI receiver blocks corresponding to the candidate receiver assumption(s) in #1 can be reported by company (optional). (if reported, companies to report how to calculate Number of FLOPs of non-AI receiver blocks as well) Note: Non-AI receiver blocks can be: channel estimation, channel interpolation, channel equalization, and demodulation/LLR calculation. (FLOPs of additional pre/post processing can be reported optionally, if any) \|<br>\| #8 Number of parameters of AI Model \| Reported by company (Backbone of AI model can be reported optionally) \|<br>\| #9 Benchmark \| Receiver: non-AI based receiver with realistic assumption Other aspects (including DMRS patterns, etc) can be reported by company The candidate benchmarks can be set as follow: Benchmark 1: Same candidate pattern of overhead-reduced DMRS for sub-case-A (e.g., sparse DMRS) Benchmark 2: Non-overhead-reduced DMRS pattern (e.g., comb-based DMRS pattern) Note: For non-AI receiver, consider realistic channel covariance matrix estimation and realistic noise-and-interference covariance matrix estimation. Note: For sub-case A, companies report at least one of two Benchmarks with the correspondent complexity. Note: For sub-case B, companies report Benchmark 2 and its correspondent complexity. Note: For Benchmark 1, at least comb-based pattern is used considering the maximum number of orthogonal DMRS port (i.e., up to 48 with X=2, where X is TD-OCC length) agreed in RAN1#126. Note: If companies report a comparison between Sub-Case A and Sub-Case B, the report must consider at least benchmark 2 with the correspondent complexity either sub-case A and/or sub-case B. Note: Companies to optionally report an approximate upper bound in performance, e.g. using ideal channel information, when reporting evaluation results. \|<br>\| #9-1 DMRS assumption for AI receiver \| reported by company \|<br>\| #10 Aspects to consider for generalization and scalability performance \| Evaluation Methodologies & Frameworks Evaluation cases 1, 2, 3 in TR 38.843 Case 1: The AI model is trained based on training dataset from one Scenario #A/Configuration #A, and then the AI model performs inference/test on a dataset from the same Scenario #A/Configuration #A. Case 2: The AI model is trained based on training dataset from one Scenario #A/Configuration #A, and then the AI model performs inference/test on a different dataset than Scenario #A/Configuration #A, e.g., Scenario #B/Configuration #B, Scenario #A/Configuration #B. Case 3: The AI model is trained based on training dataset constructed by mixing datasets from multiple scenarios/configurations including Scenario #A/Configuration #A and a different dataset than Scenario #A/Configuration #A, e.g., Scenario #B/Configuration #B, Scenario #A/Configuration #B, and then the AI model performs inference/test on a dataset from a single Scenario/Configuration from the multiple scenarios/configurations, e.g., Scenario #A/Configuration #A, Scenario #B/Configuration #B, Scenario #A/Configuration #B. Companies to report the scenarios/configurations for generalization and scalability verification, e.g., Scenario #A/Configuration #A Scenario #B/Configuration #B Generalization case Dataset mixing method (for Case 3) Note: Companies to highlight the parameter(s) to vary for generalization analysis Channel generation: considering Link Level channel and/or System Level channel (e.g., UMi, UMa) Link Level channel, if used for generating training data, shall be generated with diversified Channel & Environmental Conditions Companies can also use System Level channel to generate training data set Channel & Environmental Conditions Various Channel Types Various Channel parameters, such as various Delay Spread, various Doppler spread, various Angular Distributions Various UE speed Various SNR range Various interference level FFS: how to model interference in LLS Scheduling & System Configurations Different numbers of Tx/Rx antenna ports, MIMO layers, SU/MU-MIMO scenario, and UL precoders (TPMI) Varying time/frequency resource allocation Different MCS & Modulation, if applicable Different DMRS Configurations: DMRS pattern, sequence, time/frequency domain density Power allocation (for Sub-case B) Other aspects are not precluded, and reported by company (if needed) \|<br>\| #11a (Without considering generalization and scalability) parameters for inference \| Reported by company, considering the following aspects aNB antenna configuration UE antenna configuration Channel type Delay spread UE speed SNR range UL Precoder MCS & Modulation TDRA for PUSCH FDRA for PUSCH with PRB size (e.g., 8, 26, or 56) UL waveform (CP-OFDM or DFT-s-OFDM) Other aspects are not precluded, and reported by company (if needed) \|<br>\| #11b-1 SNR gain at BLER target without considering generalization and scalability \| Reported by company Note: Companies should also report the corresponding benchmark. Note: Gain in terms of SNR at the BLER target of PUSCH (i.e., 10%) \|<br>\| #11b-2 Tput gain without considering generalization and scalability \| Reported by company Note: Companies should also report the corresponding benchmark. \|<br>\| #11b-3 NMSE gain (if applicable) without considering generalization and scalability \| Reported by company (optional) Note: Companies should also report the corresponding benchmark. \|<br>\| #11b-4 Net gain (if applicable) without considering generalization and scalability \| Reported by company (optional) Note: Companies should also report the corresponding benchmark. \|<br>\| #12a-1 SNR gain (or loss) at BLER target considering generalization and scalability \| Reported by company Note: The gain or loss of Case 2 and/or Case 3 can be reported considering Case 1 as benchmark. Note: Gain in terms of SNR at the BLER target of PUSCH (i.e., 10%) \|<br>\| #12a-2 Tput gain (or loss) considering generalization and scalability \| Reported by company Note: The gain or loss of Case 2 and/or Case 3 can be reported considering Case 1 as benchmark. \|<br>\| #12a-3 NMSE gain (or loss) (if applicable) considering generalization and scalability \| Reported by company (optional) Note: The gain or loss of Case 2 and/or Case 3 can be reported considering Case 1 as benchmark. \| | [Chair notes RAN1#126bis_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126bis_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2607567](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Docs/R1-2607567.zip)<br>`[126bis-R20-6GR-Transmission scheme for UL channels]` |

| RAN1#124bis | 10.5.3.1 | Agreement | 6GR CSI-RS pattern is defined as aggregation of CDM groups, for which study the following aspects<br>- Whether CSI-RS pattern is defined on single or multiple slots/RBs in time/frequency domain<br>- For CDM design, consider the following options<br>  - RE locations of CDM groups<br>    - Option 1-1: Localized CDM group similar to 5G NR, where one CDM group contains adjacent REs<br>    - Option 1-2: Comb-based CDM group, where subcarriers in one CDM group are distributed following comb pattern<br>  - CDM group size and type<br>    - Option 2-1: Reuse/Simplify NR, i.e., CDM 1, 2, 4, 8 with potential reduction of candidates,<br>    - Option 2-2: Larger CDM size, e.g., CDM 16<br>    - Option 2-3: New CDM type for NR CDM size (e.g., fd-CDM4 or cdm8-FD4-TD2)<br>- At least following aspects to be considered for designing CSI-RS pattern<br>  - CSI-RS Overhead<br>  - CSI-RS coverage<br>  - CSI-RS sharing use cases<br>  - Channel estimation performance<br>  - NES<br>  - Coexistence with other signals/channels<br>  - Digital precoding/Hybrid precoding structures<br>  - MRSS | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-Aspects of DL based CSI acquisition]` |
| RAN1#124bis | 10.5.3.1 | Agreement | For the study of non-AI/AI based time domain CSI prediction at UE or NW side, consider<br>- Intermediate metric: Subband-level per layer per predicted time instance eigenvector/precoder SGCS, NMSE calculated between predicted channel and ground-truth channel<br>  - To compare NW side prediction with UE side prediction, the impact of CSI reporting shall be considered<br>  - FFS WB SGCS/NMSE<br>- System-level metric: UPT (mean, 5%tile), CSI reporting overhead<br>  - CSI-RS overhead is considered in UPT calculation<br>  - To evaluate CSI report overhead, companies to report how the PMI/channel of the predicted time instance(s) is reported<br>- Link-level metric: BLER/SE/throughput<br>- Complexity metrics: FLOPs/M<br>  - For AI based prediction: number of parameters/M<br>- Baseline: Sample & Hold<br>- Additional EVM assumption<br>  - Channel modelling: Spatial consistency with mobility procedure A<br>  - UE distribution: 100% outdoors with speed 10, 20, 30, 60, 120km/h<br>    - Other speeds are not precluded<br>  - UE Rx antenna phase discontinuity modelling: Companies to report the used model<br>  - Observation window (number/distance between adjacent CSI-RS occasions): e.g., 5/10ms, 5/20ms for periodic CSI-RS; and 12/2ms, 8/2ms, 4/2ms for aperiodic CSI-RS;<br>    - other values can be additionally submitted<br>  - Prediction window (number/length of each predicted instances/gap from the last observation instance to the 1st predicted instance):  e.g., 1/10ms/5ms, 4/10ms/5ms;<br>    - other values can be additionally submitted. | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-Aspects of DL based CSI acquisition]` |
| RAN1#124bis | 10.5.3.1 | Agreement | For the study on JSCM-based CSI compression, at least considering the following aspects on top of previous agreement for AI-based CSI compression:<br>- Performance of Projection-matrix-based compression (compress target CSI by multiplying with a projection matrix at UE) or encoder-based (e.g., transformer-based), and reconstruct the CSI at NW with a NW-sided model<br>  - Companies to report method for obtaining projection matrix/encoder<br>  - Companies to report non-AI/ML operations (if any) before/after multiplying with a projection matrix.<br>- Study the potential RF related impact (e.g., PAPR) and potential solutionsat least including<br>  - Map the output to certain discrete constellation with, at least considering<br>    - NR modulation constellations, e.g., 16QAM, 64QAM, 256QAM, 1024QAM<br>    - Other modulation constellations, e.g., 64APSK, other customized (fixed) constellations<br>  - Map/restrict the output, e.g., with restricted amplitude(s)<br>  - PAPR restriction during training as part of loss function<br>  - Note: the above operation is fixed/known by NW<br>- Both precoding matrix and explicit H can be considered as the target CSI for inference<br>- For performance evaluation related to error detection,<br>  - For benchmark of SSCC and eType II/Type I, when CSI error is detected, previous CSI is adopted to derive the precoder for downlink transmission<br>  - For JSCM, details of error detection, if any, companies report the assumption in the evaluation<br>- Study on generalization and scalability performance<br>- Study on LCM for JSCM-based CSI compression<br>- Note: Companies to report how to multiplex JSCM-compressed precoding matrix/explicit H with other UCI, e.g., RI or CQI, and/or UL-SCH<br>- Note: The related testability issue is up to RAN 4.<br>- Note: LS to RAN 4 is to be considered for RAN 4 potential related impacts, e.g., EVM, ACLR, SEM, PAPR, testability, arbitrary constellation, when mature.<br>- Note: Companies to report I/Q imbalance assumption, if any | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-Aspects of DL based CSI acquisition]` |
| RAN1#124bis | 10.5.3.1 | Agreement | For 6GR CSI-RS for DL based CSI acquisition, study CSI-RS RE sharing considering the following use cases.<br>- Use case 1: Sharing a common set or subset of REs among CSI-RS with different number of ports<br>- Use case 2: Sharing a common set or subset of REs among CSI-RS with different frequency densities<br>- Use case 3: Sharing a common set or subset of REs among CSI-RS with different periodicities/time domain types<br>- Use case 4: Sharing a common set or subset of REs among 5G CSI-RS and 6G CSI-RS<br>- Note: the combination of the above use cases can be considered.<br>- Note: the above use cases are design principles at this stage. Whether there is specification impact subjects to further discussion.<br>- Note: the scenarios for sharing of CSI-RS may need to consider CSI-RS channel estimation performance at cell-edge, precoded/non-precoded CSI-RS, AI/non-AI, NES enabled/disabled, UEs with different measurement capabilities, single-TRP/Panel or multi-TRP/Panel etc | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-Aspects of DL based CSI acquisition]` |

| RAN1#124bis | 10.5.3.1 | Agreement | For the codebook design, study at least the following codebook structures<br>- For low-resolution/ high-resolution CSI, considering ,  for evaluation<br>- Note: Other codebook structure and enhancements of NR codebook structure(s), or other codebook are not precluded<br>- Note: NR codebooks are used as benchmark for performance and complexity assessment<br>For evaluation on codebook design, companies report<br>- the max rank assumption, and whether a single codebook structure across all ranks for low-/high-resolution CSI, if appliable<br>- the assumption of SD/FD basis selection, if appliable<br>- the codebook parameter assumptions<br>- basis format assumption<br>- assumption of target CSI and corresponding codebook structure, e.g., implicit/explicit CSI<br>- complexity analysis | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-Aspects of DL based CSI acquisition]` |

| RAN1#125 | 10.5.3.1 | Agreement | For the study of non-AI/AI based CSI prediction in frequency/spatial domain at UE side, consider the following aspects<br>- Prediction input (UE side Input): reduced CSI-RS measurement<br>- Additional information to be used by UE side for CSI prediction, if applicable<br>  - Option 1: Long-term channel information derived from full-dimensional CSI-RS measurement<br>  - Option 2: Reconstruction information (indicated by BS) applied on the measured channel based on non-precoded CSI-RS,<br>  - Option 3: Reconstruction information based on precoded CSI-RS (indicated by BS), e.g., precoder applied on CSI-RS<br>  - Option 4: DMRS based CSI measurement<br>  - Other options or combination of above options are not precluded<br>  - Companies are encouraged to study whether there is performance impact caused by aging/temporary unavailability of the additional information<br>- Prediction output (UE side Output): Predicted CSI to be used for CSI report<br>  - Note: UE side Output does not necessarily equal the CSI report quantity<br>  - Companies to report the details of the predicted CSI for CSI report | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Aspects of DL based CSI acquisition]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.3.1 | Agreement | For the study on configurable/downloadable codebook/basis/bases, consider at least the following:<br>- The information for NW to determine the configurable/downloadable codebook/basis/bases, e.g., reported CPI, SRS, previous reported CSI<br>  - Companies report the detail assumptions for obtaining such information in the evaluation, at least including<br>    - Additional signaling overhead for information collection, if applicable<br>    - The assumptions of the information, e.g., the SRS related assumption, CPI reporting related assumption, time domain relationship with the target CSI report<br>    - Additional measurement overhead, if applicable<br>- Companies report<br>  - BS antenna configuration, subband configuration<br>  - signalling overhead, representing format of configurable/downloadable basis/codebook, updated frequency of the configurable/downloadable basis or configurable/downloadable codebook, how to determinate when to update<br>  - whether the configurable/downloadable codebook or basis is UE- specific or UE-common (Cell-specific), rank/layer- common or specific<br>  - codebook structure assumption for configurable/downloadable codebook/basis, e.g., eType-II-like, Type-I-like<br>  - complexity at UE side for CSI feedback with configurable/ downloadable basis/codebook for CSI feedback: e.g., number of complex operations for CSI computation and memory requirement for basis storage<br>  - whether NW-sided model is assumed<br>    - If NW-sided model is assumed, companies report the input/output, labeling.<br>- UE speed assumption follows the general EVM section 10.1 and other EVM follows the assumption agreed in RAN1#124. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Aspects of DL based CSI acquisition]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.3.1 | Agreement | For study of DMRS-based CSI, considering at least the following aspects:<br>- Potential use cases, including e.g., increased CSI accuracy including inter-layer imbalance information, CSI-RS overhead reduction, CSI acquisition for TDD.<br>- Benchmark:<br>  - CSI-RS based<br>    - P CSI-RS and/or AP CSI-RS based (precoded or non-precoded)<br>  - SRS based<br>- Company to report CSI-RS/SRS assumption for benchmark<br>- Company to report the assumptions for DMRS resources and how DMRS is used for CSI measurement, e.g., only for channel measurement or both channel and interference measurement.<br>- Companies to report the OLLA assumption details, if applicable<br>- KPI:<br>  - Throughput (average and edge UPT) vs total CSI feedback overhead (averaged over UEs, over simulation time (per time unit)), where the total CSI feedback overhead includes both DMRS based feedback, and other necessary CSI feedback (if applicable)<br>  - Note: DL RS overhead is included in throughput calculation.<br>- DMRS based report quantity:<br>  - at least CQI, companies report CQI calculation assumption<br>  - companies can report other quantities, e.g., PMI (e.g., refinement), RI, RSRP/SINR, DMRS port selection indication if assumed, including the detailed assumption<br>- UE speed assumption follows the general EVM section 10.1 and other EVM follows the assumption agreed in RAN1#124. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Aspects of DL based CSI acquisition]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.3.1 | Agreement | Support at least codebook based implicit CSI feedback in 6GR.<br>Study whether/how to support explicit CSI feedback, including at least the following aspects:<br>- Reporting quantities/format, including compression/quantization methods<br>  - e.g., full channel matrix, channel covariance matrix, eigenvector(s) with eigenvalue(s)<br>- Companies to provide reporting overhead, instance assumption for channel covariance matrix, performance and complexity analysis, and assumption for link adaptation and other reference signal (if applicable)<br>- Note: both sTRP and mTRP can be considered<br>- Note: Both AI and non-AI based solution for CSI feedback can be considered.<br>- Note: The related testability issue is up to RAN 4.<br>- Note: LS to RAN 4 is to be considered for RAN 4 testability issues, when mature. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Aspects of DL based CSI acquisition]` |

| RAN1#125 | 10.5.3.1 | Agreement | For the 6GR codebook design for CSI report, the following is considered:<br>- NR fixed DFT basis is used as a baseline for evaluation for W1 and Wf  at least for non-precoded CSI-RS<br>  - For cell-specific precoded CSI-RS, port-selection basis and/or NR DFT basis can be used as a baseline for evaluation<br>  - FFS on other basis, e.g., for near field, basis combined from DFT beams/port selection, and non-orthogonal DFT basis<br>- Low- resolution scheme:<br>  - Max RI=8 as a baseline for evaluation<br>  - Candidate structures include Type-I Scheme-A like (W1 W2), Type-I Scheme-B like (W1 W2), eType-II like L=1 (W1 W2 Wf) structures<br>    - For eType-II like L=1, layer-specific/layer-group-specific SD basis selection<br>    - Other candidate schemes are not precluded<br>  - FFS: details on whether/how to accommodate passive array with smaller number of ports<br>- High- resolution scheme:<br>  - Max RI=4 as a baseline for evaluation<br>  - eType-II L>1 (W1 W2 Wf) structure as a baseline for evaluation (including implicit and explicit feedback)<br>  - Note: Whether/how to use this for explicit channel feedback is not precluded.<br>- For both low- and high-res, CJT codebook with NTRP>1 TRPs/panels<br>  - TRP/panel specific SD basis selection, TRP/panel common FD basis selection (if applicable) as a baseline for evaluation<br>  - Study whether/how to support dynamic TRP/panel selection mechanism<br>  - Company reports the multi-TRP/panel assumption, e.g., co-located, non-co-located<br>  - Note: The term “TRP” and “panel” are used for discussion purposes<br>Note: Additional details are still to be studied, including enhancements for UPT-overhead trade-off and UE complexity | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Aspects of DL based CSI acquisition]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.3.1 | Agreement | For the study of non-AI/AI based CSI prediction in frequency/spatial domain at NW side, consider the following aspects<br>- Prediction input:<br>  - Option 1-1: UE reported channel matrix derived from reduced dimension CSI-RS measurement<br>  - Option 1-2: UE reported coefficient matrix, which is based on the multiplication of a downloaded matrix and the channel matrix derived from reduced dimension CSI-RS measurement<br>  - Option 1-3: UE reported precoding matrix derived from reduced dimension CSI-RS measurement<br>  - Option 1-4: UE reported coefficient matrix, which is based on the multiplication of a downloaded matrix and the precoding matrix derived from reduced dimension CSI-RS measurement<br>  - Other options are not precluded<br>  - Note: Performance impact caused by quantization of the UE reported CSI is part of the study<br>- Additional information to be used by NW side for CSI prediction, if applicable<br>  - Option 2-1: Long-term channel information corresponding to full dimension CSI reported by UE<br>  - Option 2-2: Channel information corresponding to full dimension CSI derived from UL measurement<br>  - Option 2-3: Channel measurement based on DL DMRS reported by UE<br>  - For spatial domain, “dimension” is defined in terms of ports<br>  - For frequency domain, companies to report the assumed granularity to define “full dimension”<br>- Prediction output: Full-dimension CSI to be used by BS<br>  - Note: companies are encouraged to report the details of the full-dimension CSI<br>- Note: companies to report the assumption of rank and MCS determination in the simulation | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Aspects of DL based CSI acquisition]` |

| RAN1#125 | 10.5.3.1 | Agreement | For the study of non-AI/AI based CSI prediction in time domain at UE side, consider the following aspects<br>- Prediction input: RS measurement from one or multiple occasions in the observation window<br>  - The RS includes at least CSI-RSs<br>  - Study the impact of RS with longer periodicity (e.g., 10ms, 20ms, for evaluation), and potential solutions, if needed<br>- Study whether additional information is beneficial for UE side time domain CSI prediction, e.g., DMRS based measurement, IMR<br>- Prediction output: CSI in the prediction window to be reported by UE<br>  - The CSI includes at least channel prediction, study whether/how to enable interference prediction<br>  - Study whether to support both N4=1 and N4>1 in the prediction window, and associated UE reporting mechanism<br>    - The definition of N4 is same as NR<br>- NR Rel-18/Rel-19 UE side CSI prediction as a start point<br>  - Study the extension to >32 ports<br>- Note: At least for CSI prediction without interference prediction, UE side time domain CSI prediction is to be compared with NW side time domain CSI prediction | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Aspects of DL based CSI acquisition]` |

| RAN1#125 | 10.5.3.1 | Agreement | For CJT calibration report,<br>- Study the following three types of reporting quantities:<br>- Inter-TRP (xTRP) delay offset, analogous to Rel-19 cjtc-Dd<br>- Inter-TRP (xTRP) frequency offset, analogous to Rel-19 cjtc-F<br>- Inter-TRP (xTRP) DL/UL phase offset, analogous to Rel-19 cjtc-P<br>- Note: Additional details are still to be studied, including dynamic range and resolution, and their additional use cases (if any)<br>- Stand-alone reporting as a baseline for evaluation<br>- Study whether/how to support reporting CJTC delay offset report and codebook-based CSI (with NTRP>1)<br>- Note: when CSI-RS and DMRS have different delay pre-compensation assumption, the potential impact on DMRS based channel estimation can be discussed in 10.5.2.2 | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Aspects of DL based CSI acquisition]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.3.1 | Agreement | For the study on channel property information (CPI), the evaluation at least considering the following:<br>Category of use cases:<br>- CSI configuration/report adaptation for overhead/complexity reduction, CSI feedback with more accuracy, and/or CSI prediction<br>- Reference signal configuration adaptation (e.g., CSI-RS for CSI, DMRS, SRS)<br>- DL/UL transmission scheduling and configuration (e.g., coordinated beamforming/scheduling for inter-TRP/cell/user interference suppression)<br>- Note: the above categories can be applicable to sTRP/mTRP.<br>Basic categories of channel properties<br>- Spatial-domain (SD)<br>- Frequency-domain (FD)<br>- Time-domain (TD)<br>- Any combination of the above domains<br>Measurement definition and/or reporting formats, for example:<br>- Correlation information (e.g., time-/frequency/spatial-domain correlation)<br>- Spectrum (e.g., channel statistics in a transform domain, basis indices and power)<br>- Channel covariance matrix<br>- Explicit channel matrix<br>- Explicit system parameters (e.g. codebook parameters, RS parameters)<br>- Other formats are not precluded.<br>Note: Strive for common report quantities for use cases, if applicable.<br>Note: The related testability issue is up to RAN 4.<br>Note: LS to RAN 4 is to be considered for RAN 4 testability issues, when mature. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Aspects of DL based CSI acquisition]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.3.1 | Agreement | For SLS/LLS evaluation for JSCM-based CSI compression,<br>- For both JSCM and SSCCM, the following Tx/Rx chain is considered.<br>Companies report the assumption and/or abstraction for each block. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Aspects of DL based CSI acquisition]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.3.1 | Agreement | For SLS evaluation for JSCM-based CSI compression,<br>- Considering the following options of the SSCCM below could be used for the SLS evaluation as a starting point:<br>  - Option 1: variable RE overhead {Throughput vs CSI feedback overhead (# of REs)}<br>    - Step 1: for SSCCM, fixed payload determination (per PC or per payload)<br>      - Different parameter combination or payload is simulated.<br>    - Step 2: CSI feedback overhead (# of REs) is averaged of scheduled UEs in SLS, and the UL resource of each UE is determined based on the UL SINR considering link adaption<br>    - Step 3(if applicable): check whether UL transmission is successfully decoded or not<br>      - Based on the PHY abstraction (flip coin) according to UL SINR for each UE<br>        - Y: Calculate UPT based on the current CSI<br>        - N: Calculate UPT based on the historical CSI<br>    - Step 4: gNB uses the received CSI feedback for DL transmission for UPT calculation across UEs.<br>  - Option 2: Fixed CSI feedback overhead (#RE) with per UE level PC/payload selection for SSCCM and per scheduling UE level uplink link adaptation for SSCCM<br>    - Step 1: Fixed CSI feedback overhead (# of REs) is used across all UEs.<br>      - Payload determination (parameter combination/payload) for each UE<br>        - Companies report how to determine the parameter commination/payload<br>      - for each UE, the payload size can be selected according to UL SINR<br>        - Companies report how to generate UL SINR, e.g., based on geometry only, or based on geometry and fast fading.<br>        - Companies report the target BLER and UL SINR definition (e.g., port domain or UL SINR after Rx combination)<br>    - Step 2 (if applicable): check whether UL transmission is successfully decoded or not<br>      - Based on the PHY abstraction (flip coin) according to UL SINR for each UE<br>        - Y: Calculate UPT based on the current CSI and update the historical CSI<br>        - N: Calculate UPT based on the historical CSI<br>  - Option 3: variable RE overhead with per scheduled UE level PC/payload selection and per scheduling UE level uplink link adaptation for SSCCM<br>    - Step 1:<br>      - Payload determination (parameter combination/payload) and link adaptation to determine the variable RE for each UE<br>        - Companies report how to determine the parameter combination/payload and link adaption<br>    - Step 2 (if applicable): check whether UL transmission is successfully decoded or not<br>      - Based on the PHY abstraction (flip coin) according to UL SINR for each UE<br>        - Y: Calculate UPT based on the current CSI and update the historical CSI<br>        - N: Calculate UPT based on the historical CSI<br>        - Note: Error free can be reported.<br>    - Step 3: gNB uses the received CSI feedback for DL transmission for UPT calculation across UEs<br>  - Other refinement to the above options are not precluded.<br>  - Other options can be reported.<br>- SSCCM baseline assumption for SLS is up to companies’ report<br>- For JSCM, CSI feedback overhead is selected for each scheduled UEs in SLS.<br>  - Companies report how to select the CSI overhead for each UE for other method.<br>- Companies report how to generate UL SINR, e.g., based on geometry only, or based on geometry and fast fading.<br>  - Companies report the uplink channel estimation error assumption.<br>- Companies report the target BLER (e.g., error free, or 1% or 10%) and UL SINR definition (e.g., port domain or UL SINR after Rx combination) for SSCCM in Step 2.<br>- Fixed max Tx power for uplink, companies report MPR assumption in the simulation. Companies report the UL power control assumption, e.g., P0 and alpha values.<br>  - PRB is used as power control adjustment granularity<br>- Companies report constellation assumption and corresponding PAPR (considering potential multiplexing with other UCI/UL-SCH).<br>- 1Tx or multiple Tx can be considered for UL. If more than 1 Tx is assumed, companies report the UL Tx/precoder assumptions.<br>- Companies report the PHY abstraction for uplink based on polar coding, if applicable.<br>- Companies report the handling of scalability of number of REs for JSCM-based CSI compression, if applicable, and whether to adopt UCI only on PUSCH or UCI with UL-SCH for benchmark and JSCM-based compression.<br>- Companies report the assumptions of JSCM, e.g., the projection-matrix-based compression (compress target CSI by multiplying with a projection matrix at UE) or encoder-based (e.g., transformer-based)<br>- Companies report the assumption on obtaining projection matrix/encoder for JSCM-based CSI compression<br>- Companies report the assumption on DL CSI-RS channel estimation error:<br>  - Error modelling in TR36.897 Table A.1-2 as a baseline if channel estimation error is modelled. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Aspects of DL based CSI acquisition]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.5.3.1 | Agreement | For the 6GR codebook design for CSI report, study a W1W2 only structure for the low-resolution scheme with the following considerations at least for RI=1-4:<br>- W1-structure<br>  - SD basis<br>    - NR oversampled 2D-DFT basis is a baseline<br>      - FFS on other basis, e.g., basis constructed from combined 2D DFT beams<br>      - FFS on alphabet set for combination coefficients for the basis constructed from combined 2D DFT beams<br>  - SD basis selection<br>    - eType-I Scheme-B like unrestricted orthogonal DFT beam selection in 2D direction is a baseline<br>      - FFS on orthogonal basis selection in at least 1D direction, or non-orthogonal basis selection<br>    - Layer-specific/layer-group-specific SD basis selection<br>      - FFS on basis-to-layer (layer-group) mapping, e.g., ordering or no ordering<br>      - FFS on the maximum number of SD basis vector selection<br>- W2-structure<br>  - Layer-specific/layer-group-specific inter-polarization co-phase selection<br>    - FFS: inter-polarization amplitude<br>  - Alphabet set for inter-polarization co-phase: BPSK, QPSK<br>    - FFS: details for each rank<br>    - FFS: for WB, whether to consider or not 8-PSK in addition to BPSK and QPSK<br>- FFS on RI>4<br>- Strive for having a unified codebook scheme for all supported ranks by 6G<br>- FFS: details on whether/how to accommodate passive array with smaller number of ports<br>- Note: UE implementation complexity is to be considered in the design of SD-basis and co-phasing selection, including the number of candidate combinations and the associated search complexity.<br>- Note: CBSR discussion will be discussed separately<br>- Note: For discussion of low resolution scheme, eType-1 Scheme-A and eType-II with L=1 are precluded | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-Aspects of DL based CSI acquisition]` |
