L>1 Layer-common SD basis selection<br>    - eType-II orthogonal DFT beam selection in 2D direction is a baseline<br>      - FFS orthogonal basis selection in at least 1D direction<br>      - FFS non-orthogonal L basis selection, e.g., basis vector- specific (q1, q2) selection<br>      - FFS orthogonal L basis selection, non-orthogonal basis selection across different layers, e.g., orthogonal DFT beam selection in 2D direction for each layer with layer-specific (q1, q2) selection<br>      - FFS whether/how to further optimize SD basis selection, e.g., using layer-common in combination with layer-specific/layer group-specific<br>- FFS whether to consider RI>4<br>- Wf-structure<br>  - eType-II layer-specific FD basis selection as a baseline<br>    - FFS on whether/how to further optimize FD compression, e.g., delay-domain pre-alignment per-basis prior to FD compression<br>- W2-structure<br>  - Linear combining (LC) coefficient scheme (ref/diff amps, phase, SCI) analogous to Rel-16 NR eType-II as a starting point<br>    - FFS: details on alphabet sets on LC coefficients<br>  - Whether to support bitmap for indicating the location of NZCs as well as a parameter for the maximum number of NZCs<br>- FFS parameter combination (PC) design<br>- Note: UE implementation complexity is to be considered in the design of SD-basis selection, including the additional complexity of inter-layer interference mitigation for layer-specific schemes. | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-Aspects of DL based CSI acquisition]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.5.3.1 | Agreement | For 6GR CSI-RS, study CSI-RS design to achieve low CSI-RS overhead considering the following possible directions<br>- Direction 1: Sparse CSI-RS in frequency/spatial domain<br>  - Consider AI and/or non-AI prediction to reconstruct the channel at UE and/or NW side<br>  - Study sparse pattern<br>- Direction 2: Use non-orthogonal CSI-RS ports<br>  - Study the use of cyclic shifts or scrambling sequences across CSI-RS RBs, or non-orthogonal cover code<br>  - Inter CSI-RS port interference leakage is to be considered in the evaluations<br>- Note: Combinations of the directions can be considered.<br>- Note: At least total CSI-RS overhead, performance and UE/NW complexity are to be studied<br>- Note: Companies to report the assumed CSI-RS time-domain behavior including CSI-RS periodicity in the evaluations<br>- Note: companies to report how CSI-RS overhead can be reduced from system perspective | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-Aspects of DL based CSI acquisition]` |

| RAN1#126bis | 10.5.3.1 | Agreement | For the study on necessity and benefit of reliability verification for JSCM-based CSI compression, study on at least the following:<br>- The purpose for reliability verification: it can be used by the NW to determinate whether to use the reconstructed CSI based on per JCSM-based CSI report<br>  - FFS the applicability to NW side performance monitoring/for LCM/error cause detection, and relationship with reliability verification (if appliable)<br>- The potential solutions, at least considering<br>  - Opt 1: with additional redundancy<br>    - Opt 1A: bit-level redundancy generated from the target CSI, e.g., perceptual Hashing, codebook-based, CRC-based<br>      - Whether the bit-level redundancy to be transmitted using conventional channel coding/modulation<br>    - Opt 1B: symbol-level redundancy generated directly (without considering bit level quantization) from the target CSI or compressed CSI output<br>    - Opt 1C: bit-level redundancy generated based on compressed CSI output symbols<br>      - Whether the bit-level redundancy to be transmitted using conventional channel coding/modulation<br>    - Opt 1D: symbol-level redundancy based on pre-known/configured signals inserted as the target input for compression, e.g., reference CSI<br>    - Opt 1E: a metric reported by UE, e.g., SGCS, generated based on target CSI and pre-known/configured reference CSI<br>      - Whether the metric to be transmitted using conventional channel coding/modulation<br>  - Opt 2: without additional redundancy (NW implementation-based)<br>    - Option 2A: based on the estimated UL SINR,<br>    - Option 2B: based on the comparison of the received (post-equalization) JSCM symbols () and the recompressed symbols (, where A is the projection matrix) from the reconstructed CSI ()<br>  - Other options or combinations of the above options are not precluded<br>- The impact on UPT (and SGCS intermediate) performance due to overhead (if any) of introducing reliability verification<br>- To evaluate the performance benefit(necessity) of above,<br>  - Study the scenarios where reliability verification has potential benefit<br>  - companies report the performance benefit, e.g., SGCS, link-level throughput<br>  - companies report along with the reliability verification, how NW determinate the precoder (e.g., fall back to previous report, NW side model selection),<br>  - companies report the details on how to identify the reliability issue. | [Chair notes RAN1#126bis_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126bis_eom1.docx)<br>`[126bis-R20-6GR-Aspects of DL based CSI acquisition]` |

| RAN1#124bis | 10.5.3.2 | Agreement | At least from the perspectives of benefit, complexity, and overhead, study the feasibility and necessity of introducing more dynamic/flexible adaptation of the following SRS parameters than that supported by NR.<br>- Frequency domain parameters, such as SRS bandwidth, starting position in frequency domain, hopping related parameters, resource element mapping<br>- Time domain parameters, such as slot offset, starting position in time domain, number of consecutive OFDM symbols, periodicity<br>- Code domain parameters, such as cyclic shift<br>- Number of SRS ports<br>- Combinations of above schemes, such as adaptive combination of comb offset and cyclic shift<br>- Spatial domain parameters, such as SRS precoding<br>- Other schemes are not excluded<br>Note 1: feasibility may be different for each of the parameters. | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-Aspects of UL based CSI acquisition]` |

| RAN1#125 | 10.5.3.2 | Agreement | Study the following cases for AI/ML UL-based CSI, and strive to support the unified SRS patterns/designs/framework that work for both AI/ML and non-AI/ML schemes.<br>- AI/ML for low-overhead SRS (Sub-Case A): low-overhead SRS with AI/ML at the network side for CSI reconstruction<br>  - Note: low-overhead SRS may include overhead reduction schemes in the time and/or frequency domains. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Aspects of UL based CSI acquisition]` |

| RAN1#125 | 10.5.3.2 | Agreement | For the evaluation of scalability/generalization of AI/ML-based UL-based CSI acquisition, the evaluation methodology in NR (as in TR 38.843) can be considered as the starting point. The set of configurations are considered focusing on one or more of the following aspects:<br>- Various antenna configurations, e.g., UE Tx port number, UE Tx port layout<br>- Various channel and link conditions, e.g., SNR/SINR ranges<br>- Various time/frequency domain factors, e.g., various frequency allocations/RPFS/hopping patterns, time domain allocations, UE speeds<br>- Other aspects, e.g., power of SRS transmission, deployment scenarios, channel models<br>Note: Companies are encouraged to evaluate generalization/scalability performance across multiple scenario/configuration combinations. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Aspects of UL based CSI acquisition]` |

| RAN1#125 | 10.5.3.2 | Agreement | For multiplexing of multiple SRS ports, study at least the following options:<br>  - TDM<br>  - CDM in frequency domains (at least include CS)<br>  - TD-OCC<br>  - FDM (at least include comb and comb offset)<br>  - Combinations of above options<br>  - Note: other schemes are not precluded<br>- Strive for a unified design framework for different numbers of ports.<br>- FFS whether/how to support dynamic/flexible adaptation of multiplexing parameters(e.g., comb and CS).<br>  - Whether/how dynamic/flexible adaptation of multiplexing parameters can be achieved beyond resource/resource-set level indication can be discussed separately | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Aspects of UL based CSI acquisition]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.3.2 | Agreement | Study at least the following aspects of SRS antenna switching for DL CSI acquisition<br>- Guard Period (GP) between consecutive SRS resources for antenna switching<br>- Whether and how to define the GP between consecutive SRS resources for antenna switching, considering the practical RF chain switching times of UEs<br>- GP between SRS and other proceeding/following UL signal/channel transmission, if different antennas are used for SRS and other proceeding/following UL signal/channel transmission,<br>- Whether/how to define GP between SRS and other proceeding/following UL signal/channel transmission<br>- Allowed combinations of x (number of Tx antennas at UE) and y (number of Rx antennas at UE)<br>- Impact of realistic UE antenna layouts (both symmetric and asymmetric number of antenna ports across RF chains)<br>- Whether/how to handle power imbalance among SRS antenna ports due to insertion loss<br>Note: regarding the practical RF chain switching times of UEs, and power imbalance, studies/conclusions from RAN4 should be considered by RAN1 | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Aspects of UL based CSI acquisition]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.3.2 | Agreement | For UL-based CSI in 6GR, study carrier switching and consider at least the following aspects<br>- Take SRS carrier switching mechanisms in NR as the starting point for 6GR carrier switching study.<br>- Strive to simplify the SRS carrier switching framework compared to NR, e.g.,<br>  - By converging the redundant triggering alternatives to reduce UE complexity and standardization overhead<br>  - By simplifying the collision handling rules when SRS for carrier switching collides with other UL signals/channels<br>  - By reducing/eliminating unnecessary switching-back | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Aspects of UL based CSI acquisition]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.3.2 | Agreement | For 6GR SRS sequence design,<br>  - candidate options including:<br>  - ZC and CGS sequences in NR<br>  - Enhanced ZC<br>  - Enhanced CGS<br>  - other directions are not precluded | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Aspects of UL based CSI acquisition]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.3.2 | Agreement | - For SRS transmission procedure to facilitate sounding in the UL of all parts of the DL bandwidth where the DL CBW is larger than supported UL CBW, study at least the following aspects/solutions<br>- UL sounding for all parts of the target bandwidth over multiple transmissions of SRS, at least consider the following for solutions<br>  - with a single SRS resource<br>  - with multiple SRS resources<br>- Consider the impacts on other signals/channels (including at least interruption of data transmission, collision handling), required number of switching, switching gap, SRS overhead to sound all parts of the DL bandwidth, time to complete the sounding<br>- Accommodating any location of UL BW, if supported<br>- Other aspects/solutions are not excluded<br>Note: studies/conclusions from RAN4 might be needed. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Aspects of UL based CSI acquisition]` |

| RAN1#126 | 10.5.3.2 | Agreement | Study whether/how TD-OCC can be supported together with SRS repetition to enable multiplexing of SRS ports, and at least take the following aspects into consideration:<br>- OCC lengths: e.g., TD-OCC2, TD-OCC4, other lengths<br>- Whether it is applicable to intra- and inter-UE multiplexing of SRS ports<br>- TD-OCC related interference randomization scheme<br>- The non-orthogonality incurred by partial dropping<br>- Channel variation in time domain | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-Aspects of UL based CSI acquisition]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.5.3.2 | Agreement | For at least increasing SRS capacity/reducing overhead/improve coverage purposes sparse SRS patterns with comb values larger than 8, study at least comb 12 and 16 with consideration of at least the following aspects.<br>  - SRS sequences<br>  - MPR and PAPR/CM impact<br>  - Max number of cyclic shifts for the corresponding comb value<br>  - Minimum available bandwidth and its corresponding sequence<br>  - Channel estimation performance<br>  - Applicable RB sizes (e.g., RB size >= 8)<br>  - Any other performance impacts<br>- FFS other comb values.<br>- Note: RAN4 input on maximum power boosting is needed | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-Aspects of UL based CSI acquisition]` |

| RAN1#126 | 10.5.3.2 | Agreement | Study at least the following aspects of precoded SRS<br>- Intended usage (e.g., for UL CSI and/or DL CSI)<br>- Feasibility under specific UE architectures (e.g., xTyR configurations for DL CSI)<br>- Gain compared to non-precoded SRS, accounting for practical impairments (e.g., PAPR/CM loss, realistic UE reciprocity, and UE coherency assumptions)<br>- Methods for precoder derivation of precoded SRS:<br>- Method-1: Determined by NW (e.g., derived from the measurements of SRS and indications from NW)<br>- Method-2: Determined (with/without reported) by UE via DL measurement<br>- FFS: UE UL/DL reciprocity calibration | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-Aspects of UL based CSI acquisition]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.5.3.2 | Agreement | For SRS of 6GR, study the following frequency hopping aspects<br>- A single-level frequency hopping<br>  - hopping over bandwidth with one or multiple frequency hops<br>- Two-level frequency hopping<br>  - First level: hopping over BW with one or multiple frequency hops<br>  - Second level: hopping within each frequency hop of the first-level hopping<br>- For single or two levels, consider at least the following options<br>  - Nested tree-like frequency hopping pattern<br>  - Sequential hopping pattern<br>  - Pattern following RB offset provided by NW<br>  - With/without Intra-repetition hopping in the second level<br>Note: the case with larger DL BW than UL BW will be discussed separately | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-Aspects of UL based CSI acquisition]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.5.3.2 | Agreement | To support maximum SRS bandwidth beyond 272 PRBs in a carrier, consider the following options:<br>- Option 1: Table based approach (similar to NR)<br>  - Option 1-1:<br>    - Refer to the bandwidth entries for up to 272 PRBs in the table from NR<br>    - Introduce new SRS bandwidth entries from 272 to [544] PRBs<br>  - Option 1-2:<br>    - Scale up the SRS bandwidth entries in the table from NR by integer factor, e.g. value of 2 or 4<br>  - Option 1-3:<br>    - The overall SRS bandwidth is divided into more than one part, in which each part can reuse SRS bandwidth entries in the table from NR.<br>- Option 2: Flexible SRS bandwidth determination and frequency hopping<br>  - Replace the existing table-based SRS bandwidth determination with parameter-based frequency hopping pattern determination provided by NW | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-Aspects of UL based CSI acquisition]` |
| RAN1#126bis | 10.5.3.2 | Agreement | For multiplexing of SRS ports per resource,<br>- Cyclic-shift (CS) based port is supported without TDM multiplexing for 2-, 3-, 4- and 8-port SRS<br>- Comb-based port multiplexing is supported without TDM multiplexing for 3-, 4- and 8-port SRS<br>- FFS the necessity of TDM multiplexing of cyclic-shift (CS) based port and comb-based port for supporting different number of SRS ports | [Chair notes RAN1#126bis_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126bis_eom1.docx)<br>`[126bis-R20-6GR-Aspects of UL based CSI acquisition]` |

| RAN1#126bis | 10.5.3.2 | Agreement | For 6GR, support SRS resource sets, each with one or multiple SRS resources.<br>- An SRS resource can be associated with multiple SRS resource sets.<br>- At least for the following SRS parameters, study whether each parameter shall be common to all SRS resources within the same SRS resource set or resource-specific:<br>  - Time domain behavior (i.e., aperiodic, periodic and semi-persistent)<br>  - Number of ports per SRS resource<br>  - Usage type<br>  - Power control related parameters | [Chair notes RAN1#126bis_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126bis_eom1.docx)<br>`[126bis-R20-6GR-Aspects of UL based CSI acquisition]` |
| RAN1#126bis | 10.5.3.2 | Agreement | Study the following combinations of comb value and cyclic shift for comb values less than or equal to 8 (assuming the minimum bandwidth = 4 PRBs for SRS in 6GR)<br>- The maximum number of cyclic shifts up to 24 for comb-2<br>- The maximum number of cyclic shifts up to 12 for comb-4<br>- The maximum number of cyclic shifts up to 6 for comb-8 | [Chair notes RAN1#126bis_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126bis_eom1.docx)<br>`[126bis-R20-6GR-Aspects of UL based CSI acquisition]` |
| RAN1#126bis | 10.5.3.2 | Agreement | Study at least the following aspects of TD-OCC:<br>- Candidate covering codes: e.g., Hadamard code, and non-Hadamard codes such as DFT code.<br>- How to design TD-OCC to support all repetition factors.<br>- The performance under partial dropping, and the feasibility of retaining orthogonality-preserved SRS ports under partial dropping, instead of dropping all ports. That is, only the SRS ports that lose orthogonality due to the dropped symbol(s) are discarded, while the remaining SRS ports that can still maintain orthogonality using the surviving symbols are retained for CSI acquisition.<br>- TD-OCC hopping for interference randomization | [Chair notes RAN1#126bis_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126bis_eom1.docx)<br>`[126bis-R20-6GR-Aspects of UL based CSI acquisition]` |

| RAN1#124 | 10.5.2.4 | Agreement | Study TCI/QCL-related aspects, e.g., definition of QCL/TCI-state, QCL property/chain<br>On beam management for DL and UL of 6GR, at least the following aspects should be studied:<br>- Beam measurement(prediction)/report/indication within a same TRP, i.e., single-TRP, in a cell/carrier;<br>- Beam measurement(prediction)/report/indication among different TRPs, i.e., multi-TRP, in a cell/carrier;<br>- Beam measurement(prediction)/report/indication among different cells/carrier, i.e., inter-cell/carrier<br>- Note: Both AI/ML and non-AI/ML related mechanism(s) for the above can be further studied.<br>Note-1: Which multi-TRP transmission scheme for study will be discussed under other agenda. | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>`[124-R20-6GR-Beam management]` |

| RAN1#125 | 10.5.2.4 | Agreement | On NW-initiated beam management, regarding DL beam measurement and report procedure on DL RS(s) for both single-TRP/cell/carrier and multi-TRP/cell/carrier scenario(s), the following aspects on DL beam measurement can be studied<br>- Study the procedure of beam sweeping considering the following alternatives:<br>  - At least support inter-symbol NW/UE-side beam sweeping including multiple DL RS(s) for DL Tx beam sweeping/repetition.<br>  - Whether/how to support the following on intra-symbol beam sweeping<br>    - Frequency-domain/FDMed at least for NW Tx beam sweeping: multiple DL RS(s) for beam measurement are multiplexed in/associated with different frequency resource(s)<br>    - Sequence-domain/CDMed at least for NW Tx beam sweeping: multiple DL RS(s) for beam measurement are multiplexed with different sequence (e.g., sequence root, or CDMed);<br>    - Sub-symbol/TDMed at least for UE Rx beam sweeping: each sub-symbol (e.g., time-domain multiplexing within a symbol) is measured by a respective Rx beam;<br>      - Note: ‘Sub-symbol’ is just for discussion purpose, which does not imply whether to introduce any new terminologies.<br>  - Note: UE-side beam sweeping is applied to the case of Rx multi-beam in FR2.<br>- Note: Granularity of DL RS can be further discussed.<br>- Study functionality requirement on DL RS measurement<br>  - Per DL measurement or across DL measurement(s), the following can be considered:<br>    - The maximum number of TRPs (within a cell or across cell)/cells/carriers<br>    - The maximum number of DL Tx beams per TRP/cell/carrier<br>    - The maximum number of DL Tx beams across measured TRPs/cells/carriers<br>- At least following aspects to be considered for designing the procedure of beam sweeping/tracking:<br>  - Increase of the number of coordinated TRPs/beams-per-TRP compared with 5G-NR<br>  - Hybrid/analog beam-forming architecture in NW<br>  - Latency/RS overhead for beam sweeping/tracking | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Beam management]` |

| RAN1#126 | 10.5.3.4 | Agreement | For the study on beam measurement and report regarding DL beam measurement and report procedure on DL RS(s) for multi-TRP scenario(s), the following can be considered on Case-1:<br>- Regarding L1-RSRP calculation, NR L1-RSRP definition can be used as the starting point.<br>  - FFS: Whether any other extension of L1-RSRP definition is needed, e.g., TRP-specific or port-specific L1-RSRP.<br>- Regarding RS measurement requirements,<br>  - Study the need of a functionality of enabling UE to a) differentiate DL RSs from different TRPs within a cell, or b) differentiate DL RSs across cells for DL beam measurement and report.<br>- Regarding report content/format,<br>  - Information of identifying DL RS can be included in the report as a starting point, besides for L1-RSRP<br>  - FFS: the following report content can be studied:<br>    - N DL RSs per selected TRP or per measured TRP<br>    - M DL RSs across different TRPs<br>  - FFS: Whether/How to include the information of selected TRP in the report.<br>  - FFS: other metrics, e.g., L1-SINR.<br>- Note (Case-1): To identify/report the preferred N>1 DL beams per NW TRP/panel or across NW TRP(s)/panel(s) for supporting multi-TRP/panel transmission scheme(s).<br>- Note: Above TRPs may belong to a same cell or different cells.<br>- Note (for the study purpose): The above study at least considers the following transmission schemes: TDMed and DPS transmission scheme, if supported. | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-Beam management]` |

| RAN1#126 | 10.5.3.4 | Agreement | Regarding UE initiated beam management, on a single-TRP operation, on UL transmission procedure, the following can be studied for Event-1 and Event-2.<br>- Candidate-1a: First UL channel + Second UL channel<br>  - First channel (e.g., PUCCH, PRACH) is to at least notify event occurrence;<br>  - Second channel (e.g., PUSCH) is to carry a beam report<br>- Candidate-1b: First UL channel + SRS<br>  - First channel (e.g., PUCCH) is to at least notify event occurrence;<br>  - SRS can be used for NW DL-Tx/UL-Rx beam determination.<br>- Candidate-2a: First UL channel at least notifying event occurrence<br>  - First UL channel can be PUCCH, PUSCH, or PRACH.<br>- Candidate-2b: SRS used for NW DL-Tx/UL-Rx beam determination | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-Beam management]` |

| RAN1#125 | 10.5.4.1 | Agreement | Study at least the following mechanisms for DCI Container size determinations at least for RRC connected state<br>- A DCI Container (defined for discussion purpose) is the physical payload that the UE attempts for decoding with a given size<br>  - no size alignment procedures across different DCI containers<br>- Alt 1: The DCI container size is implicitly determined by RRC for the DCI container, e.g., possible contents of the DCI<br>- Alt 2: The network explicitly configures DCI container size(s) via RRC<br>- Alt 3: DCI container size is pre-defined without any dependency on RRC<br>Note: the above studies are applicable for single-stage DCI and two-stage DCI<br>FFS: additional alternatives applicable for two-stage DCI only<br>FFS: maximum number of DCI container sizes for a UE<br>FFS: whether/how to do padding/truncation within a DCI container | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603880](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603880.zip)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-DL control channel and scheduling]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.4.1 | Agreement | For the study of two-stage DCI in 6GR, consider at least the following options for the physical channels/signals for the two stages:<br>- Option 1: PDCCH for both the 1st stage and 2nd stage(s), and the 2nd stage(s) use the same transmission scheme and physical resource structure as the 1st stage<br>- Option 2: PDCCH for the 1st stage,<br>  - Dedicated time/frequency domain resource for the 2nd stage(s) is indicated in the 1st stage<br>  - The 2nd stage(s) use a different transmission scheme and/or physical resource structure from the 1st stage<br>    - FFS the physical channel for the 2nd stage and how the 2nd stage is transmitted over the indicated resource<br>- Option 3: PDCCH for the 1st stage, and<br>  - If the [2nd stage/two-stage] DCI schedules PDSCH(s) carrying DL-SCH data,<br>    - 2nd stage is multiplexed on PDSCH(s) with DL-SCH data<br>      - The 1st stage indicates the time/frequency domain resource for the PDSCH(s) with DL-SCH data<br>      - FFS how the multiplexing is done<br>  - If the [2nd stage/two-stage] DCI does not schedule any PDSCH carrying DL-SCH data,<br>    - Option 3-1: Same as Option 1<br>    - Option 3-2: Same as Option 2<br>- Option 4: sequence for the 1st stage, PDCCH for the 2nd stage<br>  - Note: this is different from WUS-based PDCCH monitoring adaptation at least in the sense that whenever a two-stage DCI is transmitted, both the sequence and the 2nd stage PDCCH are always transmitted, i.e., there is a one-to-one correspondence between the 1st stage and 2nd stage.<br>  - Note: deprioritize the sequence design until more detailed design of Option 4 is available.<br>  - FFS: FAR and MDR target for the sequence<br>- Note: Polar coding is assumed except for the 1st stage in Option 4. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603881](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603881.zip)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-DL control channel and scheduling]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.4.1 | Agreement | For the study of two-stage DCI in 6GR, consider the following options for the information carried in the two stages:<br>- Option A<br>  - 1st stage DCI<br>    - Carry only the information to decode the 2nd stage DCI<br>  - 2nd stage DCI<br>    - Carry scheduling info for PDSCH(s)/PUSCH(s) and/or other downlink control information (e.g., same as single stage DCI)<br>- Option B<br>  - 1st stage DCI<br>    - Carry the information to decode the 2nd stage DCI and part of {scheduling info for PDSCH(s)/PUSCH(s) and/or other downlink control information}<br>  - 2nd stage DCI<br>    - Carry additional {scheduling info for PDSCH(s)/PUSCH(s) and/or other downlink control information} on top of those in 1st stage DCI<br>- Option C<br>  - 1st stage: a sequence indicating at least the presence of the 2nd stage DCI and/or the information to decode the 2nd stage<br>  - 2nd stage DCI: same as a single-stage DCI<br>  - Note: this option is applicable to only Option 4 of the physical channels/signals for the two stages<br>- Other options are not precluded.<br>- Note: companies are encouraged to analyse pros/cons of above options compared with single stage DCI | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603881](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603881.zip)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-DL control channel and scheduling]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.5.4.1 | Agreement | For Option 1 of the physical channels/signals for the two stages in two-stage DCI study,<br>- Same or different CORESET for the 1st stage and 2nd stage of a two-stage DCI can be considered<br>- [Same or] different SSS for the 1st stage and 2nd stage of a two-stage DCI can be considered, if SSS is supported for the 2nd stage<br>  - FFS if SSS is not supported for the 2nd stage | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2606047](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2606047.zip)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-DL control channel and scheduling]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.5.4.1 | Agreement | For Option 2 of the physical channels/signals for the two stages in two-stage DCI study<br>- Option 2-1: The 2nd-stage uses PDCCH with modifications<br>  - Same or different CORESET for the 1st stage and 2nd stage of a two-stage DCI can be considered<br>  - [Same or] different SSS for the 1st stage and 2nd stage of a two-stage DCI can be considered, if SSS is supported for the 2nd stage<br>    - FFS if SSS is not supported for the 2nd stage<br>  - Study at least the following modifications beyond what supported for 1st stage:<br>    - Additional aggregation level(s) and/or flexible position (with the granularity of CCE) of the 2nd stage<br>    - Resource determination without hash function<br>    - Higher order modulation for the 2nd stage<br>- Option 2-2: The 2nd stage uses a PDSCH transmission scheme with at least the following exceptions/restrictions<br>  - Polar code is used<br>  - QPSK is used, FFS higher order modulation<br>  - Single-layer transmission is the baseline<br>  - FFS restriction on TDRA<br>  - FFS others | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2606047](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2606047.zip)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-DL control channel and scheduling]` |

| RAN1#126 | 10.5.4.1 | Agreement | RAN1 to study at least Cell-specific, Group-specific DCI and UE-specific DCI for 6GR, with the following functions:<br>- UE-specific DCI, including:<br>  - One scheduling on DL/UL transmission by using fallback DCI  (e.g., single-layer transmission),<br>    - Applicability for RRC connected state, and FFS applicability for other RRC states.<br>  - One scheduling on DL/UL transmission by using non-fallback DCI (e.g., multi-layer transmission), where the DCI content depends on UE-specific RRC configuration;<br>  - Non-scheduling/pure control information indication<br>  - Note: a scheduling DCI can contain non-scheduling/control information<br>- Cell-specific DCI and random access procedure DCI, including:<br>  - Scheduling on common signals/channels, e.g.,<br>    - Scheduling of system information;<br>    - Scheduling of paging messages;<br>  - Scheduling on random access procedure (e.g., scheduling of Msg2/Msg4 in DL, scheduling of Msg3 retransmission· in UL);<br>  - Non-scheduling/pure control information indication<br>- Group-specific DCI, including:<br>  - Group-common information or group of UEs’ information indication.<br>- For the fallback and non-fallback DCI design, the following principles apply:<br>  - Fallback DCIs are defined for CSS<br>    - Fallback DCI does not depend on UE-specific RRC configuration;<br>    - FFS: details of CSS<br>    - Note: applicable for UE-specific RRC reconfigurations<br>  - FFS whether fallback DCIs for USS considering use cases.<br>  - Non-fallback DCI can be dependent on RRC-configurable | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2606048](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2606048.zip)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-DL control channel and scheduling]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.5.4.1 | Agreement | Study at least the following mechanisms for DCI Container size determination (at least for RRC connected state), with the details as below:<br>- For Alt 1:<br>  - the container size(s) is implicitly derived from the RRC configuration,<br>    - E.g., the size for a given DCI container is the maximum possible size based on RRC configurations for the applicable functionalities.<br>- For Alt 2:<br>  - the container size(s) are explicitly signalled by the network via RRC<br>- For Alt 3’:<br>  - DCI container size(s) is not dependent on UE-specific RRC configuration<br>    - This is e.g., cell-specific DCI and random access procedure DCI in common search space. Details FFS.<br>- FFS: Padding/reservation<br>- FFS: need for truncation<br>- FFS: need for size determination during bandwidth adaptation.<br>- Regarding UE’s DCI monitoring size budget, for a single carrier operation,<br>  - FFS: the maximum number of container sizes for a UE to monitor (e.g., for BD purpose) is Xmax.<br>  - FFS: Whether the maximum number of container sizes for a UE to monitor (e.g., for BD purpose) for UE’s RNTI (e.g., C-RNTI) is Ymax.<br>  - FFS: whether the limitation is per slot or across slots<br>  - FFS: for multi-carrier cases<br>- FFS minimum container size.<br>- FFS maximum container size.<br>- FFS maximum number of container sizes for two stage DCI<br>- Note: Using a combination of the above alternatives for different use cases is not precluded | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2606048](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2606048.zip)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-DL control channel and scheduling]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.5.4.1 | Agreement | For the evaluation of two-stage DCI vs single-stage DCI, consider at least the following DCI container sizes (not including CRC) as starting point:<br>- Single-stage DCI: 40-bit, 60-bit, 140-bit<br>- Two-stage DCI<br>  - For Option A,<br>    - 1st-stage: 20-bit if it uses PDCCH<br>    - 2nd-stage: same as single-stage DCI<br>  - For Option A,<br>    - 1st-stage: 40-bit if it uses PDCCH<br>    - 2nd-stage: same as single-stage DCI<br>  - For Option B,<br>    - 1st-stage: 40-bit if it uses PDCCH<br>    - 2nd-stage: (single-stage DCI size minus 20-bit)<br>- 24-bit CRC is the default.<br>- Other values of DCI container size are not precluded.<br>- Companies are encouraged to report used/modified assumptions, other assumptions and corresponding justifications | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2606049](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2606049.zip)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-DL control channel and scheduling]` |

It is up to companies to report what value is used for . | [Chair notes RAN1#126bis_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126bis_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2608776](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Docs/R1-2608776.zip)<br>`[126bis-R20-6GR-DL control channel and scheduling]` |

| RAN1#124 | 10.5.4.3 | Agreement | In 6GR, DL and UL HARQ operation designs considers at least the following aspects:<br>  - latency<br>  - reliability<br>  - coverage<br>  - power saving (NW and UE)<br>  - NW complexity<br>  - UE complexity<br>  - diverse services/applications/traffics<br>  - system efficiency/system throughput/user throughput<br>  - feedback efficiency/UL and DL overhead<br>Note: the design of DL and UL HARQ does not necessarily be the same | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>`[124-R20-6GR-HARQ related]` |
| RAN1#124 | 10.5.4.3 | Agreement | For DL HARQ in 6GR, study both following HARQ-ACK feedback mechanisms<br>- Mechanism 1: HARQ-ACK information bits are transmitted via L1 signalling<br>- Mechanism 2: HARQ-ACK information bits are transmitted via higher layer signalling (e.g., MAC CE) | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>`[124-R20-6GR-HARQ related]` |
| RAN1#124 | 10.5.4.3 | Agreement | For discussion purposes,<br>- Asynchronous HARQ refers to that retransmission(s) occurs in a non pre-determined occasion once the corresponding initial transmission is scheduled.<br>- Adaptive HARQ refers that the transmission parameters and resources for the retransmission can be adaptively adjusted.<br>- For DL and UL in 6GR, support asynchronous and adaptive HARQ operation. | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>`[124-R20-6GR-HARQ related]` |

| RAN1#124bis | 10.5.4.3 | Agreement | In 6GR, study whether and how to support HARQ-ACK bundling across multiple TBs | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>[R1-2603251](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Docs/R1-2603251.zip)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-HARQ related]` |
| RAN1#124bis | 10.5.4.3 | Agreement | Study HARQ-ACK codebook(s) and its operation for downlink HARQ operation in 6GR, considering at least the following aspects:<br>- HARQ-ACK codebook generation<br>- HARQ-ACK feedback granularity, e.g., TB-level, smaller than TB-level, bundling across multiple TBs, etc.<br>- Feedback overhead<br>- HARQ-ACK payload size and bits order misalignment between NW and UE due to DCI missing<br>- Ambiguity between DTX of DL assignment and PDSCH decoding failure when network decodes a NACK in a HARQ-ACK codebook<br>- Coordination between schedulers, e.g., between multiple carriers, between DL and UL, etc.<br>- Feedback complexity | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>[R1-2603253](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Docs/R1-2603253.zip)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-HARQ related]` |
| RAN1#124bis | 10.5.4.3 | Agreement | In 6GR, the minimum downlink HARQ-ACK payload size is 1 and the upper limit supported by 5G NR Polar coding can be reused (i.e., 1706 bits) at least for Mechanism 1 of HARQ feedback if supported.<br>- Note1: this upper limit does not imply the max HARQ-ACK payload size would be 1706.<br>- Note2: the exact value of the maximum size may be determined at a later stage if needed. | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>[R1-2603253](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Docs/R1-2603253.zip)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-HARQ related]` |
| RAN1#124bis | 10.5.4.3 | Agreement | In 6GR, study the details and pros and cons of the following methods to determine timing and resource for downlink HARQ-ACK feedback.<br>  - Method 1: Dynamic indication in DCI<br>  - Method 2: UE initiated HARQ-ACK feedback<br>  - Method 3: Next available/feasible time slot of semi-static configured resources that satisfy UE processing time/capability<br>  - Method 4: Only based on configuration via RRC<br>  - Note: combinations of above methods and other methods are not precluded | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>[R1-2603253](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Docs/R1-2603253.zip)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-HARQ related]` |
| RAN1#124bis | 10.5.4.3 | Agreement | For 6GR UL: Study an explicit indication or implicit indication for a given HARQ process failure to trigger faster ARQ procedure in UL.<br>- Note: Companies are encouraged to check RAN2 agreements and LS if any on fast ARQ in RAN2#133bis | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>[R1-2603326](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Docs/R1-2603326.zip)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-HARQ related]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.4.3 | Agreement | For the study on the ambiguity between DTX of DL assignment and PDSCH decoding failure in the HARQ-ACK codebook for 6GR, consider at least:<br>  - NW implementation based approach including impacts on UEs with different NW implementation if any, impact of DTX events (e.g., assuming PDCCH missed detection probability is 1%)<br>  - Self-decodable and non-self decodable PDSCH<br>  - Trade-off between additional feedback overhead and performance benefits | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2604825](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2604825.zip)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-HARQ related]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.4.3 | Agreement | For DL HARQ in 6GR, support HARQ-ACK information bits transmitted via L1 signalling (i.e., Mechanism 1).<br>- The design of DL HARQ-ACK feedback operation allows at least the possibility for the following while ensuring HARQ-ACK performance<br>  - Relaxing the need for tight coordination between schedulers (e.g., between multiple carriers, between DL and UL, etc.)<br>    - Decoupling of HARQ-ACK feedback triggering from the DL assignments scheduling the corresponding PDSCH<br>    - Other solution that addresses the same issue can also be considered<br>  - Other factors can also be considered<br>- The design of DL HARQ-ACK feedback operation allows the simplification of UL channel collision/multiplexing/transmission (e.g., resource determination) involving HARQ-ACK | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2604826](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2604826.zip)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-HARQ related]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.4.3 | Agreement | Study HARQ-ACK codebook(s) for downlink HARQ operation in 6GR, considering:<br>- HARQ-ACK codebook based on NR Type-1, NR Type-2, or NR (enhanced) Type-3 as starting point | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2604827](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2604827.zip)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-HARQ related]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.4.3 | Agreement | In 6GR, for the study of downlink HARQ-ACK feedback granularity smaller than TB-level and corresponding mechanism, consider at least the following:<br>- XOR-based retransmission feedback<br>- CB/CBG-level HARQ-ACK feedback of high-probability error patterns<br>- NR CBG HARQ-ACK feedback<br>- Codebook-based feedback<br>- Two-stage feedback<br>- 2D lattice-based CBs feedback<br>- Per-PDSCH on demand request of CBG-level feedback<br>- Mixture of TB-level and CBG-level feedback<br>- Non-uniform CB-to-CBG mapping feedback<br>- HARQ-ACK feedback enabling/disabling for some of CBGs<br>- enabling/disabling of CBG-level HARQ-ACK feedback<br>- Separate HARQ-ACK for CBs that carry MAC CEs or similar important data<br>Note: in the above applicable options, CB-level and CBG-level can be both considered.<br>Note: For the evaluation of above options, consider at least (average) feedback overhead per TB, ratio between size of retransmitted CB(s)/CBG(s) and size of original TB, and impact on DL control overhead, considering practical setup (e.g., fading channel, correlation across CBs, link adaptation, etc.)<br>Note: Companies are encouraged to check FL summary and contributions | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2604827](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2604827.zip)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-HARQ related]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.4.3 | Agreement | For Method 3 (Next available/feasible time slot of semi-static configured resources that satisfy UE processing time/capability), study details of the following:<br>- NW configures periodic UL feedback resources/timing occasions and UE feedback HARQ-ACK information for a PDSCH and/or a PDCCH associated with HARQ-ACK feedback received before a deadline in the first available UL feedback resource/timing occasion, where the deadline is determined/configured/indicated subject to UE processing time (e.g., Tproc,1) before the UL feedback resource/timing occasion.<br>Note: all 5G NR terminologies used are for discussion purpose only | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2604828](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2604828.zip)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-HARQ related]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.5.4.3 | Agreement | For Method 1 (dynamic indication of HARQ-ACK feedback timing and resource in DCI), study details of at least the following:<br>- The HARQ-ACK feedback timing and/or resource is indicated in<br>  - each DL DCI with/without scheduling corresponding PDSCH(s) with associated HARQ-ACK feedback<br>    - the DCI can provide<br>        - indication of HARQ-ACK feedback timing and/or resource with applicable values for HARQ-ACK transmission;<br>        - indication of HARQ-ACK feedback timing and/or resource can be invalid or absent (e.g., NNK1, non-numeric PRI, no field(s))<br>  - an UL DCI,<br>  - a dedicated DCI triggering HARQ-ACK feedback,<br>  - a DL DCI that schedules a PDSCH not associated with that HARQ-ACK feedback, and/or<br>  - other DCI<br>  - If the DL DCI indicates an invalid timing and/or resource or timing and/or resource are absent, then the HARQ-ACK feedback timing and/or resource is determined by one of the above or other methods<br>  - FFS: multiple HARQ-ACK feedback resources for multiple PDSCHs<br>Note: all 5G NR terminologies used are for discussion purpose only | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2604828](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2604828.zip)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-HARQ related]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.5.4.3 | Agreement | - For the study of downlink HARQ-ACK feedback granularity smaller than TB-level and the corresponding mechanism, candidate options in RAN1#125 are categorized as follow.<br>- Category A (HARQ-ACK schemes):<br>  - NR CBG HARQ-ACK feedback as comparison baseline<br>  - XOR-based retransmission feedback<br>  - CB/CBG-level HARQ-ACK feedback of high-probability error patterns / codebook-based compressed feedback<br>  - 2D lattice-based CBs feedback<br>- Category B (feedback mechanisms/procedures may be applicable on top of a Category A scheme):<br>  - Non-uniform CB-to-CBG mapping feedback<br>  - Two-stage feedback<br>  - Mixture of TB-level and CBG-level feedback<br>  - Per-PDSCH on-demand request of CBG-level feedback<br>  - Enabling/disabling of CBG-level HARQ-ACK feedback<br>  - HARQ-ACK feedback enabling/disabling for some of CBGs<br>- At least a common set of evaluation assumptions are to be determined in this meeting for Category A.<br>- FFS same/additional evaluation assumptions are to be applied for Category B. | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2606797](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2606797.zip)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-HARQ related]` |

| RAN1#126 | 10.5.4.3 | Agreement | - For study of 6G HARQ-ACK codebook based on NR Type-1 codebook as starting point, consider at least the following<br>  - Whether / how to reduce the codebook payload size<br>  - Whether / how to reduce codebook construction complexity<br>- For study of 6G HARQ-ACK codebook based on NR Type-2 codebook as starting point, consider at least the following<br>  - Whether/how to achieve additional robustness against the DCI(s) missing including last DCI(s) missing<br>  - Whether the counting / accumulating indication is confined within a cell or a set of cells<br>- For study of 6G HARQ-ACK codebook based on NR (e)Type 3 codebook as starting point, consider at least the following<br>  - Whether/how to achieve additional robustness against missing the DCI triggering the feedback<br>  - Whether / how to reduce codebook payload size<br>- FFS for each codebook type:<br>  - HARQ-ACK bit ordering<br>  - Determination of HARQ-ACK codebook payload size<br>  - For relaxing the need for tight coordination between schedulers, determine which codebook type(s) should be considered<br>  - Scheduling complexity<br>  - How to carry HARQ-ACK bits for a DCI that does not schedule a PDSCH, for at least (e)type 3 codebook<br>  - Whether/how to support standalone operation<br>- FFS: other approaches | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2606799](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2606799.zip)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-HARQ related]` |

| RAN1#125 | 10.5.5 | Agreement | RAN1 to evaluate the BSR in CB PUSCH, considering at least the following aspects:<br>- The performance of decoding a PUSCH payload when N UEs transmit in the one same time and frequency PUSCH resource with considering the following assumptions:<br>  - The N UEs use N different DMRS ports from a common pool of M (N<= M) different DMRS ports.<br>  - The N UEs use same DMRS port from a common pool of M (N <= M) different DMRS ports but with different scrambling IDs for DMRS sequence.<br>  - The N UEs use different combinations of DMRS port and scrambling ID for DMRS sequence, where the DMRS port(s) are chosen from a common pool of M(N<=M) different DMRS ports.<br>  - The N UEs could use same or different waveform for PUSCH transmission.<br>  - The N UEs use the same DMRS port from a common pool of M (N <= M) different DMRS ports and same scrambling IDs for DMRS sequence<br>- Evaluate the following aspects of CB-BSR:<br>  - Study and identify the definition of UE collision in CB PUSCH used for this evaluation and evaluate the probability of UE collision.<br>    - Companies to report the definition used in their evaluations<br>  - The L1 transmission delay of BSR in CB PUSCH.<br>    - The L1 transmission delay is the time duration between the traffic arrival and when the BSR is decoded successfully.<br>  - The CDF of the number of attempts of BSR transmission.<br>  - The complexity of blind detection at the BS side.<br>    - The evaluation can take into account that UEs uses C-RNTI or common RNTI for PUSCH scrambling and/or the number of different DMRS that is detected.<br>  - The UL resource overhead for transmitting CB BSR.<br>  - The impact of DMRS false alarm (if any).<br>  - The above study and evaluation can consider system load. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Other signals, channels, and procedures]` |

RSSI to measure the leakage of the interference, e.g., inter-subband CLI.<br>  - The frequency domain granularity for measurement to be considered are: subband and wideband.<br>- RAN1 to study the following methods of CLI measurement resources:<br>  - | RAN1#126 | 10.5.5 | Agreement | For the study of multi-bit SR for requesting UL resources in 6G:<br>- Focus the study and evaluation on the following candidate reporting content:<br>  - Quantized buffer size.<br>- Note: this candidate is for evaluation purpose only.<br>- Study and determine whether/how the reported information in multi-bit SR can assist the BS to better schedule uplink resource for the UE<br>- Study and determine for multi-bit SR:<br>  - Applicable and non-applicable scenarios for multi-bit SR, including cell load (low/high) and target packet size (small/large).<br>  - Whether and how to accommodate dynamic/flexible range of payload size of UL data.<br>  - Excess granted resource caused by buffer size quantization.<br>- Study and evaluate the required/maximal bit size and study the quantization method.<br>- With the same aggregated UL resource overhead of multi-bit SR and 1-bit SR+ scheduled PUSCH for BSR, evaluate UL transmission scheduling latency performance of multi-SR vs the mechanism of 1-bit SR + BSR (the waiting time for next SR transmission occasion is included).<br>- Evaluate the link coverage of multi-bit SR transmission in PUCCH with 1-bit SR coverage as baseline.<br>- Compare the multi-bit SR carrying quantized buffer size with the solution of using multiple 1-bit SR configurations to indicate the same target quantized buffer size, considering the resource overhead and UL transmission scheduling latency.<br>- Other candidate reporting contents can also be evaluated<br>  - E.g., delay status report, LCH/LCG ID, predicted traffic timing information. | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-Other signals, channels, and procedures]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.5.5 | Agreement | For remote interference management for 6GR:<br>- At least support wireless-based RIM framework specified in 5G/NR as starting point for 6GR.<br>  - Further study whether to support backhaul-based RIM framework.<br>- Support the following two types of RIM-RS:<br>  - RIM-RS Type 1: transmitted by victim BS to indicate the existence of remote interference<br>  - RIM-RS Type 2: transmitted by aggressor BS to detect if remote interference still exists.<br>  - The RIM RS shall carry the following information:<br>    - BS group ID<br>    - ‘Enough/Not enough’ indication in RIM-RS Type 1<br>    - ‘Near/Far’ indication in RIM RS type 1.<br>    - FFS: the RIM RS can carry 6G specific information.<br>    - FFS: the RIM RS to carry duplex specific information, e.g., TDD frame structure, SBFD  subband/symbol configuration.<br>  - FFS the time-domain and frequency domain design of RIM RS, the sequence in RIM RS, and the configuration methods of RIM RS, time location of RIM RS.<br>  - FFS whether CSI-RS can be reused as RIM RS. | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-Other signals, channels, and procedures]` |

#### 10.6.2 Uplink WUS and operation

회의별 결정 수 (하위 Agenda 포함): #122 0 · #122bis 0 · #123 0 · #124 2 · #124bis 2 · #125 5 · #126 4 · #126bis 5

| 회의 | 번호 | 구분 | 내용 | 출처 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RAN1#124 | 10.6.2 | Agreement | Study further necessity and feasibility of UL WUS under the following deployment scenario (DS):<br>- DS#1: Standalone cell where UE obtains UL WUS configuration e.g., from standalone cell and/or pre-defined in the specifications<br>  - DS#1a: Prior to UL WUS, nothing transmitted on the standalone cell<br>  - DS#1b: Prior to UL WUS, always-on 6GR synchronization signals with or without PBCH on the standalone cell but no SIB1 on the standalone cell<br>  - DS#1c: Prior to UL WUS, always-on 6GR synchronization signals with PBCH on the standalone cell and periodic SIB1 on the standalone cell<br>  - Note: UL WUS is transmitted to the standalone cell<br>- RAN1 to consider at least<br>  - Coverage target of UL WUS<br>  - How UE acquires synchronization for UL WUS<br>  - How UE decides UL WUS transmission power<br>  - RRC states for the above scenarios<br>- Note: The above scenarios can be applicable to multi-TRP deployment scenario if TRP is transparent to UE at the time of UL WUS transmission<br>- Note: The above scenarios are for study purposes only and do not imply 6GR support. | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>`[124-R20-6GR-Uplink WUS]` |
| RAN1#124 | 10.6.2 | Agreement | Study further necessity and feasibility of UL WUS under the following deployment scenario (DS):<br>- DS#2: Multi-cell/carrier where UE obtains UL WUS configuration from cell/carrier #1<br>  - Always-on 6GR synchronization signals with PBCH on cell/carrier #1, and SIB1 on cell/carrier #1<br>  - DS#2a: Prior to UL WUS, nothing transmitted on cell/carrier #2<br>  - DS#2b: Prior to UL WUS, always-on 6GR synchronization signals with or without PBCH on cell/carrier #2 but no SIB1 on cell/carrier #2<br>  - DS#2c: Prior to UL WUS, 6GR synchronization signals with PBCH on cell/carrier #2 and periodic SIB1 on cell/carrier #2<br>  - Note: UL WUS can be transmitted to cell/carrier #1 or cell/carrier #2<br>- RAN1 to consider at least<br>  - Coverage target of UL WUS<br>  - How UE acquires synchronization for UL WUS<br>  - How UE decides UL WUS transmission power<br>  - Whether the cells/carriers are in the same band or not<br>  - Whether the cells/carriers are collocated or not<br>  - RRC states for the above scenarios<br>  - Whether the above scenarios can be applicable to multi-TRP deployment scenario<br>- Note: The above scenarios are for study purposes only and do not imply 6GR support. | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>`[124-R20-6GR-Uplink WUS]` |
| RAN1#124bis | 10.6.2 | Agreement | - For study of feasibility for UL WUS, at least followings are observed for DS#1b.<br>  - For the case where prior to UL WUS, always-on 6GR synchronization signals with PBCH on the standalone cell are transmitted,<br>    - UE can acquire DL timing/frequency synchronization for UL WUS transmission at least via always-on 6GR synchronization signals and PBCH transmitted by the standalone cell.<br>  - For the case where prior to UL WUS, always-on 6GR synchronization signals without PBCH on the standalone cell are transmitted,<br>    - It is required to further study whether UE can acquire DL timing/frequency synchronization for UL WUS transmission at least via always-on 6GR synchronization signals transmitted by the standalone cell.<br>  - For both cases,<br>    - UE can determine UL WUS transmission power at least based on always-on 6GR synchronization signals transmitted by the standalone cell and information to determine UL WUS transmission power, if information is available<br>      - It is required to further study whether/how information to determine UL WUS transmission power can be delivered to UE by e.g., PBCH, predefined in spec, or other methods<br>    - It is required to further study the minimum information size/content necessary at least for UL WUS transmission/operation and how such information can be delivered to UE. | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-Uplink WUS]` |
| RAN1#124bis | 10.6.2 | Agreement | - For study of feasibility for UL WUS, at least followings are observed for DS#2b.<br>  - If UE transmits UL WUS to cell/carrier #1,<br>    - UE can acquire DL timing/frequency synchronization for UL WUS transmission at least via always-on 6GR synchronization signals and PBCH transmitted by cell/carrier #1.<br>    - UE can determine UL WUS transmission power at least based on always-on 6GR synchronization signals transmitted by cell/carrier #1 and information to determine UL WUS transmission power, if information is possibly available at least from cell/carrier #1.<br>  - If UE transmits UL WUS to cell/carrier #2,<br>    - For the case where prior to UL WUS, always-on 6GR synchronization signals with PBCH on cell/carrier #2 are transmitted,<br>      - UE can acquire DL timing/frequency synchronization for UL WUS transmission at least via always-on 6GR synchronization signals and PBCH transmitted by cell/carrier #2, or the feasibility and applicability by cell/carrier #1<br>    - For the case where prior to UL WUS, always-on 6GR synchronization signals without PBCH on cell/carrier #2 are transmitted,<br>      - It is required to further study whether/how UE can acquire DL timing/frequency synchronization for UL WUS transmission at least via always-on 6GR synchronization signals transmitted by cell/carrier #2, or the feasibility and applicability by cell/carrier #1<br>    - UE can determine UL WUS transmission power at least based on always-on 6GR synchronization signals transmitted by cell/carrier #2 and information to determine UL WUS transmission power, if information is possibly available at least from cell/carrier #1. | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-Uplink WUS]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.6.2 | Agreement | - For study of feasibility for UL WUS, at least followings are observed for DS#1c.<br>  - UE can acquire DL timing/frequency synchronization for UL WUS transmission at least via always-on 6GR SSB transmitted by the standalone cell.<br>  - UE can obtain information necessary for UL WUS transmission/operation and determine UL WUS transmission power at least via always-on 6GR SSB and periodic SIB1 and/or RRC signaling transmitted by the standalone cell. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Uplink WUS]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.6.2 | Agreement | - For study of feasibility for UL WUS, at least followings are observed for DS#2c.<br>  - If UE transmits UL WUS to cell/carrier #1,<br>    - UE can acquire DL timing/frequency synchronization for UL WUS transmission at least via always-on 6GR SSB transmitted by cell/carrier #1.<br>    - UE can obtain information necessary for UL WUS transmission/operation and determine UL WUS transmission power at least via always-on 6GR SSB and periodic SIB1 and/or RRC signaling transmitted by cell/carrier #1.<br>  - If UE transmits UL WUS to cell/carrier #2,<br>    - UE can acquire DL timing/frequency synchronization for UL WUS transmission at least via always-on 6GR SSB transmitted by cell/carrier #2.<br>    - UE can obtain information necessary for UL WUS transmission/operation and determine UL WUS transmission power at least via always-on 6GR SSB and periodic SIB1 and/or RRC signaling transmitted by cell/carrier #2. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Uplink WUS]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.6.2 | Agreement | - For study of feasibility for UL WUS, at least followings are observed for DS#2a.<br>  - If UE transmits UL WUS to cell/carrier #1,<br>    - UE can acquire DL timing/frequency synchronization for UL WUS transmission at least via always-on 6GR SSB transmitted by cell/carrier #1.<br>    - UE can determine UL WUS transmission power at least based on always-on 6GR synchronization signals transmitted by cell/carrier #1 and information to determine UL WUS transmission power, when information is available at least from cell/carrier #1.<br>  - If UE transmits UL WUS to cell/carrier #2,<br>    - UE can acquire DL timing/frequency synchronization for UL WUS transmission at least via always-on 6GR SSB and/or periodic SIB1 transmitted by cell/carrier #1, if cell/carrier #1 and cell/carrier #2 are co-located and synchronized. Otherwise, it is required to further study how to acquire DL timing/frequency synchronization.<br>    - UE can determine UL WUS transmission power at least based on always-on 6GR synchronization signals transmitted by cell/carrier #1 and information when available at least from cell/carrier #1, if cell/carrier #1 and cell/carrier #2 are co-located and synchronized. Otherwise, it is required to further study the feasibility and how to determine UL WUS transmission power and/or transmission beam.<br>- Scenario where UE moves from cell/carrier #1 to cell/carrier #2 (where cell/carrier #1 may not provide underlay coverage for cell/carrier #2) and can maintain DL timing/frequency synchronization and UL WUS configuration for a certain period of time is part of DS#2a<br>  - it is required to further study the feasibility and how to maintain DL timing/frequency synchronization and UL WUS configuration for a certain period of time.<br>- It is required to further study triggering conditions for UE to transmit UL WUS for cell/carrier #2, given that no DL signals/channels are available from cell/carrier #2.<br>- Note: Whether cell/carrier #1 and cell/carrier #2 are synchronized follows RAN4 definition. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Uplink WUS]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.6.2 | Agreement | - For study of feasibility for UL WUS, at least followings are observed for DS#1a.<br>  - Majority companies expressed the concern that UE cannot discover the cell or UE cannot acquire DL timing/frequency synchronization for UL WUS transmission even with the assistance of GNSS, while some companies claimed that GNSS (if applicable) can be used for GNSS-capable UE to derive timing information and acquire frequency synchronization for UL WUS transmission.<br>  - Majority companies expressed the concern that UE cannot determine UL WUS transmission power without DL signals by the standalone cell, while some companies claimed that UE can use pre-configured or pre-defined parameters for UL power control for UL WUS transmission. Some companies indicated that pre-configured or pre-defined parameters for UL WUS transmission power may lead to excessive interference and BS/UE energy consumption. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-Uplink WUS]` |

| RAN1#126 | 10.6.2 | Agreement | - For feasibility study of DS#1b, further study the following mechanisms for UE to acquire UL WUS configuration.<br>  - Option 1: Pre-configuration and/or pre-defined in specification<br>  - Option 2: Synchronization signal(s)<br>  - Option 3: PBCH including PBCH DMRS<br>  - Option 4: Broadcast PDSCH<br>  - Option 5: Common PDCCH<br>  - Note: Combination of above options can be considered.<br>  - At least the followings are considered for further study of the above options<br>    - NW configuration flexibility<br>    - NW and UE energy saving/consumption<br>    - UE complexity<br>    - Signaling overhead<br>    - Necessary payload by taking SIB26 for NR OD-SIB1 as the reference | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-Uplink WUS]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.6.2 | Agreement | - For study of necessity for UL WUS, at least followings are considered as candidates of use cases.<br>  - For UEs in idle mode,<br>    - UE-initiated on-demand or adaptation procedures for one or multiple of the following signals/channels:<br>      - 6GR SS/PBCH<br>      - 6GR SIB1<br>      - 6GR PRACH<br>      - 6GR DL Reference Signal<br>  - For UEs in connected mode,<br>    - UE-initiated on-demand or adaptation procedures for one or multiple of the following signals/channels:<br>      - 6GR SS/PBCH<br>      - 6GR SIB1<br>      - 6GR PRACH<br>      - 6GR DL Reference Signal<br>    - UL data indication (including ‘no UL data’ indication)<br>    - Selection of PUSCH resource and/or PUSCH transmission parameter<br>    - UL WUS based measurement<br>    - Indication of new beam for BFR (if supported for 6GR)<br>- With consideration of at least the following aspects:<br>  - 6GR SSB/SIB1 periodicity/repetition<br>  - Coverage<br>  - UL WUS detection performance<br>  - NW and UE energy/power consumption<br>  - Latency<br>  - NW and UE complexity<br>  - Resource overhead<br>  - Necessity of UE-triggered operation compared to NW-triggered mechanisms<br>  - Which DS(s) are applicable to the above use cases<br>  - Interference aspects<br>  - Inter-node coordination<br>  - Overlapping with existing or other 6GR mechanisms that could play the same functionalities | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-Uplink WUS]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.6.2 | Agreement | - For study of feasibility for UL WUS, followings are observed for DS#2a in addition to previous RAN1 agreement.<br>  - If UE transmits UL WUS to cell/carrier #2, and if cell/carrier #1 and cell/carrier #2 are non-co-located,<br>    - UE can determine UL WUS transmission power as the pre-defined TX power (e.g., maximum TX power) Further study<br>      - Whether/how to mitigate interference to the cell/carrier other than cell/carrier #2<br>      - Whether/how to handle the impact to UL WUS detection performance<br>      - Whether UE can determine path-loss estimation from cell/carrier #1 DL signals and power offset value provided by cell/carrier #1 when available/applicable.<br>        - Details on how to use path-loss estimation from cell/carrier #1 DL signals<br>    - UE can use wide/omni-directional beam or beam sweeping as UL WUS transmission beam. Further study<br>      - How to handle the impact of reduced cell coverage, when using wide/omni-directional beam.<br>      - How to determine narrow beam and whether/how to mitigate interference to the cell/carrier other than cell/carrier #2.<br>    - UE can use cell/carrier #1 SSB as timing reference for UL WUS transmission when cell/carrier #1 and cell/carrier #2 are synchronized when the timing can be maintained in UE, or when cell#1/carrier #1 provides underlay coverage for cell#2/carrier #2.<br>    - It is required to further study whether/how UE can use cell/carrier #1 SSB as timing reference for UL WUS transmission or not, when cell/carrier #1 and cell/carrier #2 are not synchronized, considering inter-cell distance, timing advance, etc.<br>    - This can cover the scenario where UE moves from cell/carrier #1 to cell/carrier #2 (where cell/carrier #1 may not provide underlay coverage for cell/carrier #2) and can maintain DL timing/frequency synchronization and UL WUS configuration for a certain period of time<br>      - It is required to further study the duration of the certain period of time with coordination with RAN4 as needed | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-Uplink WUS]` |

| RAN1#126 | 10.6.3 | Agreement | - For the study of any information carried in DL-WUS with or, if supported, without the wake-up indication, RAN1 to at least use the following common assessment criteria:<br>  - Complexity of the UE EE processing and NW’s impact (if any);<br>  - Coverage impact of the resulting payload;<br>  - DL (and, where applicable, UL) resource overhead;<br>  - Energy-saving benefit at both UE side and network side, and latency impact;<br>  - Overlapping with existing or other 6GR mechanisms that could carry the same information<br>  - Whether DL-WUS used for other functions is beneficial than the existing or other 6GR mechanisms<br>  - The agreed FAR/FDR/MDR for DL WUS are used as the threshold for FAR/FDR/MDR of the additional (non-wake-up) information and associated functionality. | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-WUS operation with other functionalities]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.6.3 | Agreement | - For UEs in RRC_IDLE / RRC_INACTIVE state, RAN1 to study at least the following candidate additional functions for DL-WUS:<br>  - Candidate #1: SI-modification and/or ETWS-CMAS notification carried via DL WUS.<br>  - Candidate #2: Use DL-WUS as a trigger or indication for on-demand and/or additional RS and/or common signals/channels, if supported.<br>  - Candidate #3: Use DL-WUS to indicate PF/PO resources or RACH occasions that can be used.<br>  - Candidate #4: Study DL WUS to trigger Downlink Small Data Transmission (DL SDT) in inactive state, if supported. | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-WUS operation with other functionalities]` |
| RAN1#126bis | 10.6.3 | Agreement | - For UEs in RRC_CONNECTED state, RAN1 to study at least the following candidate additional functions for DL-WUS,<br>  - Candidate-1: Interaction between DL-WUS and Cell DTX or Cell DRX,<br>  - Candidate-2: DL-WUS interacts with ‘Cell/Carrier Dormancy/(De)activation’ Operation<br>  - Candidate-3: Use DL-WUS as a trigger or indication for on-demand and/or additional RS and/or common signals/channels and/or CSI report, if supported.<br>  - Candidate-4: Study DL-WUS to indicate throughput reduction for subsequent active time<br>  - Candidate-5: DL WUS carries acknowledgement information (ACK/NACK) in response to a UE request for UL data transmission<br>  - Candidate-6: DL WUS indicating beam parameter/TCI update<br>  - Candidate 7: DL-WUS triggers DL-SPS PDSCH reception.<br>  - Candidate 8: DL-WUS activates/de-activates CG-PUSCH transmission.<br>  - Note: 5G NR design is assumed as starting point and further RAN1 and RAN2 progress on relevant features are considered, if applicable.<br>Note: Interaction between DL-WUS and PDCCH monitoring adaption (at least including ‘SSSG switching’ / monitoring-config selection, PDCCH skipping, ‘PDCCH BD reduction’) are to be handled under AI 10.6.1.2. | [Chair notes RAN1#126bis_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126bis_eom1.docx)<br>`[126bis-R20-6GR-WUS operation with other functionalities]` |
