| RAN1#126 | 10.7.1 | Agreement | In 6GR NTN, under the label of “physical layer aspects of multi-satellite operation”, the following sub-aspects are studied under “physical layer aspects related to inter-satellite interference management”<br>- Co-channel interference, taking into account characteristics of NTN channels (e.g. large and time-varying Doppler / timing offsets due to orbital dynamics)<br>  - At least for LEO same orbit.<br>  - FFS other parameters (e.g. elevation angle)<br>- NOTE: It is assumed that the UE is only connected to one satellite at a time. | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2606422](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2606422.zip)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-NTN specific requirement and design]` |
| RAN1#126bis | 10.7.1 | Agreement | At least the following parameters for satellite assistance info for UL time-frequency pre-compensation are supported for feeder link in 6GR NTN (at least for GNSS-based operation):<br>- Common TA<br>- Common TA drift rate<br>- Common TA drift rate variation<br>- For the feeder link in a transparent payload case UE assumes one of the following alternatives.<br>  - Alt 1: The feeder link Doppler is fully pre-compensated by the NW as in NR-NTN Rel-17.<br>  - Alt 2: The feeder link Doppler is pre-compensated by the NW in a way that, over the DL on service link, the observed time drift rate matches the observed frequency error.<br>  - Decide which alternative. | [Chair notes RAN1#126bis_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126bis_eom1.docx)<br>`[126bis-R20-6GR-NTN specific requirement and design]` |
| RAN1#126bis | 10.7.1 | Agreement | In 6GR NTN, it is supported that UEs with different GNSS operation modes can operate simultaneously in the same cell.<br>- Network functionality is introduced to control access from UEs in different GNSS operation modes (e.g. to only allow UEs in a given GNSS operation mode to access the cell).<br>  - FFS: Which combination of GNSS operation mode(s) are allowed to be simultaneously enabled in the same cell.<br>  - FFS: Details<br>- NOTE: The operation modes are:<br>  - GNSS-based<br>  - GNSS-degraded<br>  - GNSS-free/GNSS-less | [Chair notes RAN1#126bis_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126bis_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2608593](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Docs/R1-2608593.zip)<br>`[126bis-R20-6GR-NTN specific requirement and design]` |
| RAN1#126bis | 10.7.1 | Agreement | For the 6GR NTN GNSS-less/free/degraded study, the solutions for UE pre-compensation recommended for specification in TR 38.742 are taken as starting point (except for PRACH physical channel which is discussed in the common agenda):<br>- For open loop uplink time and frequency pre-compensation:<br>  - For scenarios where UE cannot rely on its GNSS for UL timing and frequency pre-compensation on the service link, based on assistance information from the network.<br>  - For cases where last known GNSS location is available and still sufficiently valid, this location is used for uplink open-loop time and frequency pre-compensation<br>    - FFS: How “sufficiently valid” is defined<br>- Frequency adjustment command (in connected mode and RAR)<br>- TA command enhancements at least in RAR<br>- TA drift (e.g. based on FAC)<br>- NOTE: Adjustments to the solutions in TR 38.742 can be proposed based on other decisions taken for 6GR. | [Chair notes RAN1#126bis_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126bis_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2608593](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Docs/R1-2608593.zip)<br>`[126bis-R20-6GR-NTN specific requirement and design]` |
| RAN1#126bis | 10.7.1 | Agreement | For 6GR NTN, further study the following options regarding channel/signal assignment to wide/narrow beams for hierarchical beam structure.<br>- Option 1:<br>  - Use wide beams (in DL) for SSB, common PDCCH, SIBs, paging<br>  - Use narrow beam for PRACH reception at aNB<br>    - Proponents to clarify how the UE selects the PRACH resource for different GNSS operating modes.<br>  - Use narrow beams for dedicated channels (DL + UL)<br>- Option 2:<br>  - Use wide beams (in DL) for SSB<br>  - Use narrow beams (in DL) for common PDCCH, SIBs and paging<br>  - Use narrow beam for PRACH reception at aNB<br>    - Proponents to clarify how the UE selects the PRACH resource for different GNSS operating modes.<br>  - Use narrow beams for dedicated channels (DL + UL)<br>- Option 3:<br>  - Use same beam (wide or narrow) for SSB, common PDCCH, SIBs, paging, PRACH reception at aNB during initial access.<br>  - Hierarchical beam structure is only applied for channels after PRACH reception<br>    - | RAN1#125 | 10.8.1 | Agreement | For object detection and/or tracking, define velocity accuracy for 6G ISAC evaluation:<br>Velocity accuracy is defined as the absolute value of the difference between the estimated velocity and the corresponding true velocity of a sensing target. For single node monostatic sensing or single pair of bistatic sensing, both the radial velocity accuracy and the 3D velocity accuracy can be estimated. The true radial velocity is the sum of the following two components:<br>- Component 1: The projection of the velocity difference vector on the unit-norm vector from target to STX, where the velocity difference vector is between the true 3D velocity of the target and the true 3D velocity of the STX;<br>- Component 2: The projection of the velocity difference vector on the unit-norm vector from target to SRX, where the velocity difference vector is between the true 3D velocity of the target and the true 3D velocity of the SRX.<br>Note: If STx and SRx are static, true radial velocity is , where  is the true 3D velocity of the target,  is the bistatic angle between incident direction and scattering direction, and  is the angle between the true 3D velocity vector and the bisector vector within the bistatic angle . For mono-static sensing, . | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603926](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603926.zip)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-ISAC-Evaluations]` |

| RAN1#125 | 10.8.1 | Agreement | For Rel-20 6G ISAC evaluation on communication assistance, the following SAC (sensing assisted communication) evaluation scope is considered:<br>- Further discuss the sensing measurement/result used to assist communication, which may include, e.g.:<br>  - Delay/Doppler/angle/power/phase related information of the ISAC channel<br>  - Information of detected objects (static or moving) and/or large size surface (e.g. EO type-2)<br>- Further discuss evaluation of the performance of sensing measurement/results, which are used to assist communication.<br>  - Scenario: At least Urban Grid is considered<br>    - Urban Grid with or without EO type-2 can both be considered<br>    - Other scenarios are not precluded.<br>  - FFS detailed evaluation assumptions, sensing modes, prior information of EO-type2, etc.<br>  - When evaluated, company should report:<br>    - Performance metrics on sensing measurement/result used to assist communication<br>    - How such sensing measurement/result is able to assist the communication<br>    - The corresponding performance of sensing measurement/results<br>- Further discuss evaluation of communication performance assisted by sensing.<br>  - SAC use cases that observed in AI 10.8.2 can be considered<br>  - When evaluated, company should use the same scenario/assumptions (and ISAC channel if applicable) as sensing performance evaluation.<br>  - When evaluated, company should clarify whether ideal/non-ideal sensing measurement/result is used to assist communication.<br>  - When evaluated, company should report:<br>    - Communication-related performance metrics<br>    - Detailed methods on how the sensing measurements/results assist the communication<br>    - The corresponding communication performance gain/loss<br>Note: Strive for minimizing/no extension on existing channel model. It is up to company to use chapter 7/8 of TR38.901 for communication performance evaluation. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603928](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603928.zip)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-ISAC-Evaluations]` |

| RAN1#126 | 10.8.1 | Agreement | For Rel-20 6G ISAC evaluation on SAC (sensing assisted communication), companies are encouraged to evaluate and report at least one of the following:<br>- Scope 1: Evaluate performance of sensing measurement/result, which will be used to assist communication;<br>- Scope 2: Evaluate performance of communication, with and without assistance of sensing measurement/result. The sensing measurement/result to assist communication can be:<br>  - Ideal sensing measurement/result<br>  - Non-ideal sensing measurement/result, and company to report how to model error/offset of non-ideal factors for non-ideal sensing measurement/result<br>  - Real sensing measurement/result, which is obtained from simulation<br>  - Note: companies to report which is used in their simulation.<br>For Rel-20 6G ISAC evaluation on SAC, for Scope 2:<br>- The communication use case(s) in AI 10.8.2 are encouraged<br>- Companies to report whether the location and/or velocity information of communication UE and/or TRP is needed or not in their SAC algorithm/mechanism<br>  - Note: this does not imply specifying exchange of location and/or velocity information between UE and TRP<br>- Companies to report the time-frequency resource cost due to sensing for SAC and necessary details on the definition of the time-frequency resource cost based on TR38.765 as starting point<br>  - Comparison with benchmark and benchmark details should also be reported as well as other necessary details if any<br>- Companies are encouraged to use communication-related performance metrics as agreed in communication agendas<br>- Companies are encouraged to use baseline/benchmark mechanism as agreed in communication agendas for comparison; Use of state-of-the-art mechanism without assistance of sensing measurement/result for comparison is not precluded<br>- Companies are encouraged to use additional communication-related evaluation assumptions (if necessary but not discussed/agreed in AI 10.8.1) as agreed in communication agendas<br>Note: How to draw conclusion/observation is a separate discussion. | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2605743](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2605743.zip)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-ISAC-Evaluations]` |

RMSE of power of the path(s) used to assist communication<br>      - FFS: details on the power of the path(s)<br>    - FFS: RMSE of phase of the path(s) used to assist communication<br>    - Companies to report how to select the path(s), how to derive RMSE from multiple paths and how such sensing measurement/result of the paths(s) is able to assist communication<br>    - Note: If STx and SRx are static, true radial velocity is , where is the true 3D velocity of the target, is the bistatic angle between incident direction and scattering direction, and is the angle between the true 3D velocity vector and the bisector vector within the bistatic angle . | RAN1#126bis | 10.8.1 | Agreement | For Rel-20 6G ISAC performance evaluation, for sensing assisted communication, for reporting the time-frequency resource cost due to sensing for SAC:<br>- Type_1: Resource that are used for sensing purpose (due to sensing for SAC)<br>- Type_2: Part of Type_1 resources that are used for communication purpose<br>- Type_3: Resources that are not used for sensing purpose, and cannot be used for communication purpose due to sensing operation (due to sensing for SAC)<br>Companies are required to report Overhead 1 and Overhead 2.<br>- Overhead 1: (Type_1 + Type_3) resources over all radio DL and UL resources<br>- Overhead 2: (Type_1 - Type_2 + Type_3) resources over all radio DL and UL resources<br>Note: If Type_2 resource doesn’t exist, two overheads are the same; if Type_1 resource = Type_2 resource, Overhead 2 is equal to Type_3 resource only, which could be zero if Type_3 doesn’t exist.<br>Note 2: Overhead 1 and Overhead 2 should be calculated in NW level, not single UE level.<br>Note 3: For some of the communication use cases, the communication resource overhead may be reduced due to sensing assistance, which will be reported separately, e.g. as performance metric of communication<br>Note 4: Type_2 resource shall be calculated excluding the reduced communication resource overhead if the communication resource overhead can be reduced due to sensing assistance.<br>Companies can report additional information/assumption on whether/how much the SAC resource can be shared with OD&T.<br>Note 5: This does not require companies to simulate OD&T and SAC simultaneously<br>Note 6: This does not imply specifying same or different RS/resource for OD&T and SAC | [Chair notes RAN1#126bis_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126bis_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2607430](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Docs/R1-2607430.zip)<br>`[126bis-R20-6GR-ISAC-Evaluations]` |

| RAN1#124bis | 10.8.2 | Agreement | - On measurement report for ISAC, study at least the following aspects and applicable scenarios (e.g., sensing modes, targets, etc.) from RAN1 perspective.<br>  - Measurement reporting mechanism from UE<br>    - Option 1A: The UE measurements and/or assistance information if needed from UE can be directly sent to aNB<br>    - Option 1B: The UE measurements and/or assistance information if needed from UE can be sent to SF<br>  - Measurement reporting mechanism from aNB<br>    - Option 2A: The aNB measurements and/or assistance information if needed from aNB can be directly sent to UE<br>    - Option 2B: The aNB measurements and/or assistance information if needed from aNB can be sent to SF<br>  - The study may require cross-WG coordination.<br>  - Note: combination of multiple options is not precluded.<br>  - Note: measurements in each option may be different | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>[R1-2602591](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Docs/R1-2602591.zip)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-ISAC-Integration]` |
| RAN1#124bis | 10.8.2 | Agreement | - On measurement report for ISAC, study impacts from at least the following aspects from RAN1 perspective<br>  - Measurement reporting mechanism<br>    - E.g., Periodic, semi-persistent, aperiodic, event-triggered report as starting point<br>    - Reporting signaling e.g., L1, L2, higher layer, etc.<br>  - Other aspects are not precluded<br>  - The study may require cross-WG coordination. | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>[R1-2602591](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Docs/R1-2602591.zip)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-ISAC-Integration]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.8.2 | Agreement | - Study ISAC in all 6GR frequency ranges<br>- Study ISAC using each individual sensing mode<br>- Study ISAC using the combination of multiple sensing modes from RAN1 perspective | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603994](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603994.zip)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-ISAC-Integration]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.8.2 | Agreement | - On time domain phase continuity for sensing RS, study at least the following aspects.<br>  - Definition of CPI<br>  - Factors that impact phase continuity in a CPI<br>  - Whether/how to maintain phase continuity in a CPI?<br>  - Whether/how to recover phase continuity in a CPI?<br>  - Impacts on sensing measurement/reporting<br>  - Other aspects are not precluded<br>- Companies are encouraged to bring up evaluation results including considered measurement and potential spec impacts on phase continuity issues in RAN1#126, e.g., the tolerable phase discontinuity. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603994](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603994.zip)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-ISAC-Integration]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.8.2 | Agreement | - For study on resource multiplexing within sensing and between sensing and communication, consider at least the following aspects.<br>  - TDM/FDM/CDM/SDM/PDM (power domain multiplexing) multiplexing within sensing and between sensing and communication<br>  - Collison handling or signal sharing within sensing and between sensing and communication<br>  - Other aspects are not precluded | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603994](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603994.zip)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-ISAC-Integration]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.8.2 | Agreement | - RAN1 should identify at least one representative use case of sensing assisted communication for study in Rel-20<br>  - RAN1 to study the potential impacts if any on physical layer design for sensing assisted communication beyond what is necessary for object detection/tracking use-cases for UAV/human/Vehicle/AGV.<br>  - FFS: physical layer design aspects are limited to the scope of AI10.8 | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603995](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603995.zip)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-ISAC-Integration]` |

| RAN1#125 | 10.8.2 | Agreement | - Study the necessity, scenarios and related physical layer specification impacts of UE power control/TRP power allocation for RS used for sensing considering both sensing performance and impacts to communication | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603996](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603996.zip)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-ISAC-Integration]` |

| RAN1#125 | 10.8.2 | Agreement | - Study the necessity, scenarios and related physical layer specification impacts of interference handling for sensing, to mitigate the interference within sensing and between sensing and communication, taking interference handling for communication as starting point. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603996](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603996.zip)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-ISAC-Integration]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.8.2 | Agreement | - For study the necessity, scenarios and related physical layer specification impacts of sensing RS resource allocation, consider at least the following aspects.<br>  - Frequency resource allocation for sensing resource that may or may not be different from the frequency resource allocation for communication<br>  - Other aspects are not precluded | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603996](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603996.zip)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-ISAC-Integration]` |
| RAN1#125 | 10.8.2 | Agreement | Further study following options for evaluation of RE pattern of RS for sensing in addition to theoretical RE pattern characteristics analysis.<br>- Option 1<br>  - Full SLS as 10.8.1:<br>    - All evaluation assumptions/metrics/KPI agreed in 10.8.1 are reused<br>- Option 2<br>  - SLS with non-cooperative sensing (i.e., no fusion)<br>    - All evaluation assumptions/metrics agreed in 10.8.1 are reused except<br>      - LOS condition is always assumed for each STX-target-SRX link<br>      - FFS other simplification<br>- Option 3<br>  - SLS with single STX and single SRX<br>    - Evaluation assumptions/metrics agreed in 10.8.1 are reused except<br>      - LOS condition is always assumed for each STX-target-SRX link<br>      - FFS other simplification<br>- Option 4 (same way as 10.8.3)<br>  - Companies are encouraged to provide either LLS or a simplified SLS. It’s up to company to select and how to model LLS or a simplified SLS. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2603997](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2603997.zip)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-ISAC-Integration]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.8.2 | Working Assumption | - The following representative use cases for sensing assisted communication is/are selected for study in Rel-20 ISAC<br>  - Sensing assisted beam management<br>  - [Sensing assisted CSI acquisition and reporting]<br>  - Note: companies can also study other use cases for sensing assisted communication<br>- Note: In AI10.8, physical layer design discussions are limited to sensing related aspects | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2605585](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2605585.zip)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-ISAC-Integration]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.8.2 | Agreement | In addition to theoretical characteristics analysis, companies are encouraged to do at least one of followings to evaluate RE pattern of sensing RS in 10.8.2<br>- Full SLS with or without cooperative sensing as 10.8.1 (Option 1 from RAN1#125) for sensing performance evaluation<br>- SLS with non-cooperative sensing (i.e., no fusion) (Option 2 from RAN1#125) at least for sensing measurement performance evaluation<br>      - LOS condition is always assumed for each STX-target-SRX link<br>- Simplified SLS with single STX and single SRX (Option 3 from RAN1#125) at least for sensing measurement performance evaluation<br>      - LOS condition is always assumed for each STX-target-SRX link<br>- Note: detailed modelling is up to company report | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2605586](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2605586.zip)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-ISAC-Integration]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.8.2 | Agreement | Study on a sensing RS resource consisting of one or multiple component RS.<br>- Study the following options for component RS<br>  - Component RS can be RS for communication is reused for sensing<br>  - Component RS can be enhanced RS for sensing, taking reuse of RS for communication as starting point<br>  - Component RS can be dedicated RS for sensing<br>- Note: The multiple component RS of a sensing RS resource can be of single or multiple RS types.<br>- Companies to provide necessity, theoretical analysis, performance evaluation and specification impacts on the above options and the sensing RS resource in next RAN1 meetings.<br>- Note: RE pattern of the sensing RS resource is union set of all REs of all component RS<br>- FFS: details of component RS | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2605586](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2605586.zip)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-ISAC-Integration]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.8.2 | Agreement | Study the following two options to generate a sensing RS resource<br>- Option 1: A sensing RS resource has single antenna port, which can be precoded or non-precoded<br>- Option 2: A sensing RS resource can have multiple antenna ports, which can be precoded or non-precoded<br>- Companies to provide necessity, theoretical analysis, performance evaluation and specification impacts on the above options in next RAN1 meetings.<br>- FFS impact on measurement reporting and assistance information | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2605586](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2605586.zip)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-ISAC-Integration]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.8.2 | Conclusion | - On UE-side measurement report, measurement Level A from NR ISAC is not considered for 6G ISAC study in Rel-20. | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2605587](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2605587.zip)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-ISAC-Integration]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.8.2 | Agreement | - The following metrics for a path are to be studied in 6G ISAC<br>  - Delay information defined per path<br>    - Option 1: Receive time difference between a path and a reference path, e.g., RSTD like<br>    - Option 2: Receive time difference between a path and a reference time, e.g., RTOA like<br>      - FFS reference time<br>    - Option 3: Receive time of a path minus a transmission time, e.g., Rx-Tx time difference like<br>      - FFS transmission time<br>  - Doppler information defined per path<br>    - FFS absolute or relative/differential Doppler information<br>  - Angle information defined per path<br>    - FFS absolute or relative/differential angle information, implicit/indirect angle information<br>    - FFS how to derive angle<br>  - RSRP/SINR/amplitude/phase defined per path<br>    - FFS how to derive phase<br>  - Quality/uncertainty/confidence defined per path<br>  - FFS ambiguity handling of delay/Doppler/angle of a path<br>  - Further discuss the additional metrics for a path<br>    - Micro-Doppler<br>    - RCS<br>    - Association among paths<br>    - Other metrics are not precluded<br>  - FFS reference path<br>  - FFS definition of path<br>- Note: the necessity, applicable sensing modes, achievable sensing performance, reporting aspects (e.g., overhead) of above metrics can be discussed separately | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2605587](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2605587.zip)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-ISAC-Integration]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.8.2 | Agreement | - The following metrics of a scattering point or an object are to be studied in 6G ISAC from RAN1 perspective<br>  - 3D or 2D location<br>    - Option1: Absolute location<br>    - Option2: Relative location referred to a reference location<br>    - FFS reference location<br>  - 3D or 2D velocity<br>    - Option1: Measured true 3D/2D velocity<br>    - Option2: Scalar of radial velocity<br>  - Uncertainty/confidence<br>  - association of measurements of a scattering point/object<br>  - FFS ambiguity handling of delay/Doppler/angle of a scattering point<br>  - Further discuss the additional metrics for a scattering point/object<br>    - Power related information if applicable, e.g., RCS<br>    - Micro-Doppler<br>    - Other metrics are not precluded<br>  - FFS definition of scattering point/object<br>- Note: the necessity, applicable sensing modes, and achievable sensing performance, reporting aspects (e.g., overhead) of above metrics can be discussed separately | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2605587](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2605587.zip)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-ISAC-Integration]` |
| RAN1#126 | 10.8.2 | Agreement | - The metrics of consecutive samples in delay/Doppler/angle profiles are to be studied in 6G ISAC<br>  - FFS: whether/how to apply window(s) of consecutive samples in delay/Doppler/angle profile<br>- Note: the necessity, applicable sensing modes, and achievable sensing performance, reporting aspects (e.g., overhead) of above metrics can be discussed separately | [Chair notes RAN1#126_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2605588](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126/Docs/R1-2605588.zip)<br>`[126-R20-6GR-ISAC-Integration]` |
| RAN1#126bis | 10.8.2 | Agreement | - The following interference types need to be studied for 6G ISAC, which are dependent on sensing modes and sensing scenarios.<br>  - Self-interference (for the case where mono-static is involved)<br>  - The interference between sensing signals<br>  - The interference between sensing and communication<br>- Companies are encouraged to bring up evaluation results on potential interference issues.<br>  - E.g., what is interference source, in which sensing mode, performance difference with/without interference are recommended for the study.<br>- If interference issue for sensing needs to be resolved, the following aspects of interference control can be studied in Rel-20, taking interference handling for communication as starting point.<br>  - Coordinated resource allocation in time/frequency/code/spatial domain, including e.g., measurement/transmission gap/window<br>  - Resource muting<br>  - Rate matching<br>  - Power control<br>  - Interference resource/measurement/report<br>  - Implementation method<br>  - Other aspects are not precluded | [Chair notes RAN1#126bis_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126bis_eom1.docx)<br>`[126bis-R20-6GR-ISAC-Integration]` |
| RAN1#126bis | 10.8.2 | Agreement | - Study at least the following beam related aspects for Rel-20 ISAC taking communication beam management as starting point, to identify whether sensing specific enhancement on beam related aspects for sensing is necessary or not<br>  - Measurement/report/information to determine best Tx-Rx beam pair(s) for sensing<br>  - QCL/TCI state or spatial-relation assumptions of sensing RS | [Chair notes RAN1#126bis_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126bis_eom1.docx)<br>`[126bis-R20-6GR-ISAC-Integration]` |
| RAN1#126bis | 10.8.2 | Agreement | - Study at least the following aspects of open loop power control of UE as sensing transmitter using existing SRS power control framework as starting point, to identify whether sensing specific enhancement on power control for sensing is necessary or not<br>  - P0/alpha<br>  - PCMAX<br>  - Power boosting<br>  - Pathloss/Pathloss reference<br>  - PH/PHR<br>  - Association of the applicable power-control parameters for sensing purpose<br>  - UE transmission power within CPI<br>  - the impact/interference to communication and sensing<br>- Companies are encouraged to bring up evaluation results on potential power control issues. | [Chair notes RAN1#126bis_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126bis_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2607231](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Docs/R1-2607231.zip)<br>`[126bis-R20-6GR-ISAC-Integration]` |
| RAN1#126bis | 10.8.2 | Working Assumption | - RAN1 adopts the following definition on nominal Coherent Processing Interval (CPI) for discussion purpose<br>  - “nominal CPI”: The time interval for sensing measurements during which the sensing RS resource can be coherently processed unless intolerable phase discontinuity and/or power inconsistency happens.<br>    - FFS: in nominal CPI, the sensing RS resource can be coherently processed in time domain only or in other domain as well<br>    - FFS: whether/how both transmitter and receiver have information on nominal CPI<br>    - FFS: solutions to maintain/recover the phase continuity and/or power consistency in a nominal CPI<br>    - FFS: details on intolerable phase discontinuity and/or power inconsistency<br>  - Note: the use nominal CPI in RAN1 discussion doesn’t necessarily mean such terms will be specified in normative phase | [Chair notes RAN1#126bis_eom1](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23126bis_eom1.docx)<br>[R1-2607231](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_126b/Docs/R1-2607231.zip)<br>`[126bis-R20-6GR-ISAC-Integration]` |
| RAN1#126bis | 10.8.2 | Agreement | The following options can be considered for further study on the delay measurement of a path of path-based measurement or of a sample of profile-based measurement.<br>- Option 1: Receive time difference between a path/sample and a reference path/sample,<br>  - is the receive time defined by the path/sample<br>  - is the receive time defined by the reference path/sample<br>    - FFS Candidates of reference path/sample<br>- Option 2: Receive time difference between a time of path/sample and a reference time,<br>  - is the receive time defined by the path/sample<br>  - is reference time. FFS reference time<br>- Option 3: Receive time of a path/sample of a node minus a transmission time of the same node,<br>  - is the receive time defined by the path/sample<br>  - is a transmit timing. FFS transmit timing<br>- [Option 4: Receive time of a path/sample minus a transmission time,<br>  - is the receive time defined by the path/sample<br>  - is a transmit timing. | RAN1#124 | 10.5.0 | Agreement | For the 6GR smallest maximum UE bandwidth for at least one lower-tier device, RAN1 to further study the following alternatives:<br>- Alt 1: 20MHz RF and BB bandwidth for both UL and DL with 15kHz SCS for FDD, and with 30kHz SCS for TDD<br>- Alt 2: 5MHz RF and BB bandwidth for FDD with 15kHz SCS for both UL and DL, 10 or 20 MHz RF and BB bandwidth for TDD with 30kHz SCS for both UL and DL<br>- Alt 3: 20MHz RF bandwidth for both UL and DL with 15kHz SCS for FDD, and with 30kHz SCS for TDD<br>  - Narrower bandwidth for BB in UL, and/or Narrower bandwidth for BB in DL | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>`[124-R20-6GR-General, Synchronization and Beam Measurement]` |
| RAN1#124 | 10.5.0 | Agreement | For the RAN1 study of “Re-use of existing 5G mid-band (~3.5 GHz) site grid for 6G deployments in at least around 7 GHz and targeting comparable to same coverage to 5G mid-band”,<br>- For the link budget evaluation for coverage gap identification in around 7 GHz<br>  - For initial access, Rel-15 NR signals/channels during initial access are used for identifying the gap of individual signal/channel compared to Rel-15 NR msg3 in 5G mid-band, respectively<br>- Note: The candidate coverage enhancement techniques will be separately discussed. | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>`[124-R20-6GR-General, Synchronization and Beam Measurement]` |
| RAN1#124 | 10.5.0 | Agreement | For 6GR spectrum aggregation operation, study the following methods and their associated application scenarios:<br>- Method 1: Multiple physical carriers can be aggregated into single “Gothia cell”<br>  - Note: the term ‘Gothia cell’ is for RAN1 discussion purposes, and whether/how to specify the feature / refer to the feature is separate RAN1 discussion.<br>- Method 2: “Carrier aggregation” where multiple physical carriers can be aggregated into separate cells<br>- For both methods, study them under idle mode and connected mode, and study their pros and cons at both NW and UE side | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>`[124-R20-6GR-General, Synchronization and Beam Measurement]` |

| RAN1#124bis | 10.5.0 | Agreement | For the RAN1 study of “Re-use of existing 5G mid-band (~3.5GHz) site grid for 6G deployments in at least around 7 GHz and targeting comparable coverage to 5G mid-band”, if link budget template candidates 1 is used to calculate the metric(s), the coverage gap between ~7GHz and 5G mid-band is calculated as follows<br>Coverage gap = MPL1 – MPL2 – PL_diff [– additional margin]<br>  - [FFS: detailed value of additional margin]<br>Note:<br>- MPL1: MPL of the evaluated signal/channel in ~7GHz<br>- MPL2: MPL of the bottleneck channel in 5G mid-band (e.g., Rel-15 NR Msg3 for initial/random access procedure)<br>- PL_diff = 20*log10(f1 / f2), where f1 and f2 are the carrier frequency for ~7GHz and 5G mid-band, respectively | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-General, Synchronization and Beam Measurement]` |
| RAN1#124bis | 10.5.0 | Agreement | RAN1 to discuss beamforming gain for DL broadcast channel and UL channel and to align the interpretation of the following parameters in link budget template candidate 1<br>- (4b) Antenna gain correction factor at antenna gain component 3 & antenna gain component 4 of transmitter (dB)<br>- (5b) Antenna gain correction factor at antenna gain component 2 of transmitter (dB)<br>- (11b) Antenna gain correction factor at antenna gain component 3 & antenna gain component 4 of receiver (dB)<br>- (11bis-b) Antenna gain correction factor at antenna gain component 2 of receiver (dB)<br>- (15) Receiver interference density<br>- (27) Penetration margin (dB): Whether account for the indoor distance in the pathloss calculation in O2I scenarios<br>- (25) Shadow fading margin (function of the cell area reliability and lognormal shadow fading std deviation) (dB): Function definition and whether handoff gain is accounted | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-General, Synchronization and Beam Measurement]` |
| RAN1#124bis | 10.5.0 | Agreement | For the RAN1 study of “Re-use of existing 5G mid-band (~3.5GHz) site grid for 6G deployments in at least around 7 GHz and targeting comparable coverage to 5G mid-band”, companies are encouraged to at least provide the link budget results for the following signals/channels during initial access in around 7GHz:<br>- DL:NR PSS/SSS, SSB, Common PDCCH, SIB1 PDSCH, Msg2/4 PDSCH<br>- UL:NR PRACH format C2/B4/0, MSG3 PUSCH, MSG5 PUSCH (companies to report assumption of the payload of actual transmission),  MSG4 PUCCH Format 1<br>- The simulation assumptions in section A.1 in TR38.830 are used as a starting point.<br>  - The payload for NR SIB1 PDSCH is 1200 bits.<br>  - FFS: other parameters | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-General, Synchronization and Beam Measurement]` |
| RAN1#124bis | 10.5.0 | Agreement | From frequency domain resource mapping perspective, study TB/CB/CBG mapping within a PDSCH with frequency domain resource allocation between 200MHz and 400MHz considering the following options:<br>- Option A: A TB can span up to 400MHz<br>- Option B: A TB can span up to 200MHz<br>  - FFS details<br>Note: For both options, whether multiple TBs are time domain multiplexed within a PDSCH due to other restrictions will be separately discussed in agenda item 10.5.2.2. | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-General, Synchronization and Beam Measurement]` |
| RAN1#124bis | 10.5.0 | Agreement | For the study of link direction determination for dynamic TDD, consider the following options:<br>- Option 1:<br>  - TDD pattern is based on DL, UL and flexible symbols<br>  - TDD pattern is semi-statically configured<br>  - No dynamic slot format indication as in NR<br>  - For dynamically scheduled single transmission/reception in flexible symbols, UE link direction is determined only based on scheduling DCI<br>  - Study transmissions/receptions without associated DCI in flexible symbols (if configured)<br>- Option 2:<br>  - Semi-statically configured TDD pattern is based on DL, UL and flexible symbols<br>  - Dynamically indicated TDD pattern is based on DL, UL and guard symbols<br>    - Dynamically indicated TDD pattern indicates DL, UL or guard symbols for flexible symbols according to semi-statically configured TDD pattern<br>    - The TDD pattern should be provided to the UE with sufficient processing time to apply the TDD pattern change<br>  - UE link direction is determined based on TDD pattern<br>- Option 3:<br>  - TDD pattern, based on DL, UL and guard symbols (i.e. no flexible symbols)<br>  - UE is dynamically indicated with a TDD pattern out of predefined/preconfigured TDD pattern<br>    - The TDD pattern should be provided to the UE with sufficient processing time to apply the TDD pattern change<br>- Other options are not precluded | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-General, Synchronization and Beam Measurement]` |
| RAN1#124bis | 10.5.0 | Agreement | For the 6GR smallest maximum UE bandwidth for at least one lower-tier device, RAN1 agrees the following observations for the alternatives agreed in RAN1#124:<br>- According to NR Rel-18 eRedCap study for a device supporting a single FDD band with spectrum allocation no smaller than 20MHz, when comparing on the basis of same PHY peak rate (~10 Mbps), the additional UE modem complexity reduction of Alt 2 compared with Alt 1 is ~10%, and the additional UE modem complexity reduction of Alt 3 compared with Alt 1 is ~5%.<br>HD-FDD 1-Rx UE modem complexity reduction estimates from the eRedCap SI<br>\| Closest RAN1#124 alternative for smallest maximum 6G UE bandwidth \| Modem complexity reduction option in eRedCap SI TR 38.865 \| Modem complexity reduction relative to eRedCap Option PR1 (Alt 1) \|<br>\| Alt 1 \| Option PR1 \| 0% \|<br>\| Alt 2 \| Option BW1 \| 10% \|<br>\| Alt 3 with 5 MHz BB for all channels \| Option BW2 \| 7% \|<br>\| Alt 3 with 5 MHz BB for PxSCH only \| Option BW3 \| 4% \|<br>FD-FDD 1-Rx UE modem complexity reduction estimates from the eRedCap SI<br>\| Closest RAN1#124 alternative for smallest maximum 6G UE bandwidth \| Modem complexity reduction option in eRedCap SI TR 38.865 \| Modem complexity reduction relative to eRedCap Option PR1 (Alt 1) \|<br>\| Alt 1 \| Option PR1 \| 0% \|<br>\| Alt 2 \| Option BW1 \| 8% \|<br>\| Alt 3 with 5 MHz BB for all channels \| Option BW2 \| 5% \|<br>\| Alt 3 with 5 MHz BB for PxSCH only \| Option BW3 \| 4% \|<br>- Placeholder for companies to provide more UE complexity analysis based on inputs to RAN1#125, e.g., multi-band devices | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-General, Synchronization and Beam Measurement]` |

| RAN1#125 | 10.5.0 | Agreement | For the 6GR smallest maximum UE bandwidth for at least one lower-tier device for FDD with 15kHz SCS:<br>- Reasons for possible recommendation of 20MHz RF and BB bandwidth for both UL and DL (i.e. Alt 1) include:<br>  - If initial access is independent of UE’s bandwidth capability, which requires initial access for both DL and UL to be contained within 20MHz and 5 MHz for Alt 1 and Alt 2 respectively even for FDD bands with spectrum allocation larger than 5MHz, Alt 1 allows both the lowest-tier device and MBB devices to operate in the same band with better system performance in terms of DL coverage assuming same PSD and capacity for initial access, paging and random access compared with Alt 2.<br>    - For Alt 2, it results in lower performance for initial access for 6G MBB UEs compared to 5G MBB UEs, since 5G networks can configure a bandwidth larger than 5 MHz for initial access. But such DL coverage losses might be mitigated by techniques such as power boosting.<br>  - The additional UE modem complexity reduction of Alt 2 compared with Alt 1 is no more than 10% when the same number of duplexers/SAW-filters/switches is considered for all alternatives<br>  - In case of a multi-RAT device, UE modem complexity reduction of Alt 2 compared with Alt 1 may not be exploitable in all implementations, e.g. when the other RAT requires supporting a 20 MHz bandwidth.<br>  - Alt. 1 can reach the minimum PHY peak data rate within a larger DL coverage assuming same PSD by using a lower MCS in 20 MHz CBW compared with Alt. 2 but in that case a bandwidth larger than 5MHz has to be used.<br>- Reasons for possible recommendation of 5MHz RF and BB bandwidth for both UL and DL (i.e. Alt 2)  include:<br>  - Alt 2 achieves ~8-10% additional UE modem complexity reduction compared with Alt 1 for a device supporting single FDD band<br>  - 5MHz BW is feasible for all device types for initial access, paging and random access for FDD based on previous study and deployment experience<br>    - More scheduling flexibility is offered by Alt 1 compared with Alt 2 if initial access is common to all device types, when the available bandwidth is larger than 5 MHz in an FDD band if an operator wants to operate both lowest-tier and MBB UEs in the same band. UL scheduling flexibility loss can be partially mitigated if fast frequency retuning (1-2 symbols) can be supported by lowest-tier UEs.<br>- Reasons for possible recommendation of 20MHz RF bandwidth for both UL and DL, and 20MHz BB bandwidth for DL and 5MHz BB bandwidth for UL (i.e. Alt 3 with only BB BW reduction for UL) include:<br>  - If initial access is independent of UE’s bandwidth capability, which requires initial access for both DL and UL to be contained within 20MHz and 5 MHz for Alt 3 and Alt 2 respectively and UL transmission is limited to 5MHz within each symbol for Alt 3 even for FDD bands with spectrum allocation larger than 5MHz, Alt 3 allows both the lowest-tier device and MBB devices to operate in the same band with better system performance in terms of DL coverage assuming same PSD and capacity for initial access, paging and random access compared with Alt 2.<br>    - For Alt 2, it results in lower performance for initial access for 6G MBB UEs compared to 5G MBB UEs, since 5G networks can configure a bandwidth larger than 5 MHz for initial access. But such DL coverage losses might be mitigated by techniques such as power boosting.<br>  - The additional UE modem complexity reduction of Alt 2 compared with Alt 3 (with only BB BW reduction for UL) is no more than 7% for a device supporting single FDD band<br>  - The additional UE modem complexity reduction of Alt 3 (with only BB BW reduction for UL) compared with Alt 1 is less than 4% for a device supporting single FDD band.<br>  - Alt. 3 can reach the minimum PHY peak data rate within a larger DL coverage assuming same PSD by using a lower MCS in 20 MHz CBW compared with Alt. 2 but in that case a bandwidth larger than 5MHz has to be used.<br>- For all the three alternatives,<br>  - There are more 5MHz spectrums than 20MHz spectrums in sub-1 GHz bands available for lowest-tier devices, although some operators may only have spectrums larger than 5MHz for lowest-tier devices<br>  - For a device supporting multiple FDD bands, equipped with multiple band-specific analogue filters (duplex filters for FD-FDD, SAW filters for HD-FDD), when comparing on the basis of same PHY peak rate (~10 Mbps) and same number of band-specific analogue filters, the additional UE modem complexity reduction of Alt 2 and Alt 3 compared to Alt 1 is less than for single band device.<br>  - For HD-FDD UL, five sources in RAN1 [R1-2603776][R1-2603941][R1-2604259][R1-2604548] [R1-2605059] observe that elimination of band-specific SAW filters can provide a substantial (~ 30-60%) modem complexity reduction for multi-band devices.<br>    - RAN1 understands that multiple options are under discussion in RAN4 to support SAW-less UE implementation.<br>    - The feasibility and benefits of different RAN4 options to facilitate supporting SAW-less UE implementation for different RAN1 smallest maximum UE bandwidth alternatives is up to RAN4.<br>    - The outcome of the RAN4 study may have implications for the RF and/or BB bandwidth for HD-FDD UL. | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-General, Synchronization and Beam Measurement]` |

### 10.7.1 NTN specific requirements and design for GNSS based operation (마지막: RAN1#125)

| RAN1#124 | 10.7.1 | Agreement | RAN1 will define evaluation parameters for at least the following combinations of satellite orbit and bands:<br>- S-band:<br>  - LEO 300, LEO 600, GEO<br>- Ka band:<br>  - [LEO 300], LEO 600, [LEO 1200], GEO<br>- Ku band:<br>  - LEO 1200, GEO<br>NOTE 1: The evaluations for S band are expected to be similar to L-band.<br>NOTE 2: This is only for the purpose of evaluations. | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2601469](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2601469.zip)<br>`[124-R20-6GR-NTN specific]` |
| RAN1#124 | 10.7.1 | Agreement | RAN1 to use the following terminology when discussing GNSS availability at least for physical layer operation.<br>- GNSS-based: Refers to the network mode of operation which relies on devices being equipped with a GNSS receiver and the devices can obtain a position fix within a given accuracy<br>  - FFS: How often the UE may be required to obtain a position fix, which may be related to the required accuracy.<br>  - FFS: if position under this operation can be obtained by means other than GNSS that provides a comparable accuracy, e.g. pre-configuration for a fixed device. This may also include information other than positioning.<br>- GNSS-degraded: Refers to the network mode of operation which relies on devices being equipped with a GNSS receiver, the devices were able to obtain a position fix at some point in time, but the devices may not currently have a position fix within a given accuracy.<br>  - NOTE: The UE may be able to use the position fix for physical layer operation<br>- GNSS-free/GNSS-less: Refers to the network mode of operation which does not rely on devices being equipped with a GNSS receiver, or devices are equipped with a GNSS receiver but do not have a current position fix that can be used for physical layer operation. | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2601469](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2601469.zip)<br>`[124-R20-6GR-NTN specific]` |
| RAN1#124 | 10.7.1 | Agreement | 6GR NTN targets to support GNSS-based operation, GNSS-degraded operation and GNSS-less/GNSS-free operation. | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2601470](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2601470.zip)<br>`[124-R20-6GR-NTN specific]` |
| RAN1#124 | 10.7.1 | Agreement | 6GR NTN uplink time-frequency synchronization follows the same principle as NR NTN as baseline:<br>- The concept of “uplink synchronization reference point” is introduced in 6GR NTN.<br>- 6GR NTN provides satellite assistance information<br>- At least for GNSS-based operation, it is supported that UE uses its own location information + satellite assistance information to perform time-frequency pre-compensation. | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2601470](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2601470.zip)<br>`[124-R20-6GR-NTN specific]` |
| RAN1#124 | 10.7.1 | Conclusion | As a general principle for 6GR NTN study:<br>- Under NTN agenda item, we will identify issues / requirements specific to NTN.<br>- Potential solutions to these issues / requirements may be studied under the NTN agenda<br>  - The outcome of this study may be discussed under other agenda items if common design is possible.<br>  - These solutions may end up resulting in an extension of the TN design.<br>  - This may depend on the solution / issue / requirement<br>- NTN specific solutions may be introduced when a common / extended design cannot meet the NTN requirements.<br>- When targeting a common design TN performance is prioritized. | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2601470](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2601470.zip)<br>`[124-R20-6GR-NTN specific]` |
| RAN1#124 | 10.7.1 | Agreement | 6GR supports large scheduling offsets to accommodate the RTT introduced by the satellite channel. Further discuss how to realize these scheduling offsets:<br>- Option 1: Reuse the k_offset concept from NR as a baseline with potential modifications.<br>  - NOTE: Under this option, additional scheduling offsets (e.g. similar to K1/K2 in NR) may be supported for scheduling flexibility, which apply in addition to k_offset.<br>- Option 2: The large scheduling delays to accommodate the RTT are incorporated into the scheduling offsets (e.g. similar to K1/K2 in NR), which may or may not be common for TN and NTN | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2601471](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2601471.zip)<br>`[124-R20-6GR-NTN specific]` |
| RAN1#124 | 10.7.1 | Conclusion | When reporting inputs for the link budget template and evaluation assumptions to RAN1#124b, companies are encouraged to provide them in an xls attached to their contribution following the format of the xls attached to R1-2601471. | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2601471](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2601471.zip)<br>`[124-R20-6GR-NTN specific]` |
| RAN1#124 | 10.7.1 | Agreement | Study NTN specific issues/requirements at least for the following aspects for 6GR NTN under this agenda:<br>- Uplink time-frequency synchronization<br>- HARQ issues: e.g. enable/disable HARQ feedback (which may include how to efficiently operate with HARQ feedback enabled/disabled), number of HARQ processes, etc.<br>- Timing relationships with large RTT.<br>- Coverage target<br>- Physical layer aspects of multi-satellite operation (including multi-orbit)<br>- Aspects related to Multiple beams per satellite<br>- Aspects related to satellite having more beam footprints than simultaneously active beams<br>Other aspects are not precluded. | [Chair notes RAN1#124 - eom_03](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124%20-%20eom_03.docx)<br>[R1-2601471](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124/Docs/R1-2601471.zip)<br>`[124-R20-6GR-NTN specific]` |
| RAN1#124bis | 10.7.1 | Agreement | For the issue of HARQ stalling due to large RTT in NTN, study the following solutions (which may or may not have specification impact), including their applicability:<br>- Solution 1: HARQ feedback disabling.<br>- Solution 2: PDSCH / PUSCH transmissions that span multiple slots.<br>- Solution 3: aNB reusing the same HARQ process before receiving HARQ-ACK feedback for the previous transmission<br>- Solution 4: Sufficient number of HARQ processes<br>- Note: Combination of solutions above can be considered.<br>- FFS: Whether the above techniques can be harmonized with TN | [Chair notes RAN1#124bis_eom5](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_124b/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23124bis_eom5.docx)<br>`[124b-R20-6GR-NTN specific]` |

| RAN1#125 | 10.7.1 | Agreement | For 6G NTN, RAN1 to evaluate solutions for satellite having more beam footprints than simultaneously active beams by reporting the following for a given combination of {hierarchical beam structure scheme, default SSB periodicity}:<br>- Coverage ratio for common channels, obtained as per Rel-19 methodology as (N2/(N1 + N2)) assuming N3=0.<br>- Resource overhead of common channels.<br>- Impact on link budget and cell acquisition latency (e.g. for a single sync raster point).<br>- Impact (from RAN1 perspective) on measurements<br>- NOTE: Details on assumptions for this evaluation (e.g. percentage of simultaneous active beams for UL and DL, calculation of cell acquisition latency, link budget, what common channels and their configuration are included for the resource overhead, etc.) will be separately discussed, and can be reported by companies until RAN1 can reach an agreement.<br>- Companies to report details on the proposed hierarchical beam structure scheme and default SSB periodicity, including at least:<br>  - Details on hierarchical beam structure scheme include at least the following:<br>    - Assumed beam structure (e.g. wide/narrow beam, including the assumed beamwidth for the different beams), for both UL and DL.<br>    - What channels / signals are transmitted in the different beams.<br>    - Peak EIRP / antenna gain of the different beams<br>    - Beam illumination pattern for the different beams (e.g. TDM between wide/narrow beam)<br>    - Methodology for calculation of N1/N2<br>  - Details on default SSB periodicity include at least the following:<br>    - Beam illumination scheme for different signals / channels.<br>    - SSB periodicity value.<br>- NOTE: The above does not imply that hierarchical beam structure is only relevant for cases where the satellite has more beam footprints than simultaneously active beams<br>- NOTE: Structure of NR signals / channels can be initially used for evaluation until other agenda items progress on the 6GR signals / channel structure.<br>NOTE: The Rel-19 agreement including the definition of N1/N2/N3 is as follows:<br>\| For system level study based on analytical evaluation: N1 beam footprints are in state “off” These beam footprints are not served by any signal (no satellite service in this area) N2 beam footprints are in state “common messages only” These beam footprints do not have any active user traffic, and are served the necessary information for cell discovery and initial access. Optionally, companies may consider user arrival (e.g. RACH access) in this type of cell, and should describe how this is taken into account in the analytical evaluation N3 beam footprints are in state “active traffic” These beam footprints have X active (e.g. VoNR) users each. These beam footprints are also served the necessary information for cell discovery and initial access N1 + N2 + N3 = “Total number of beam footprints “ N1, N2, N3, X are to be reported by companies. Resource utilization obtained under the assumptions above is to be reported by companies. Other assumptions made in the evaluation are to be reported by companies, e.g. power sharing scheme, beam hopping scheme, etc. \| | [Chair notes RAN1#125_eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23125_eom.docx)<br>[R1-2604768](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_125/Docs/R1-2604768.zip)<br>`[125-R20-6GR-NTN specific]` |

| RAN1#123 | 11.2 | Agreement | For FTP Model 3, the packet delay budget (PDB) can be additionally considered,<br>- The latency characteristic of the traffic in RAN side (i.e., air interface) is modelled as packet delay budget (PDB). The PDB is a limited time budget for a packet to be transmitted over the air from a BS to a UE for DL, or from a UE to a BS for UL.<br>- For a given packet, the delay of the packet incurred in air interface is measured from the time that the packet arrives at the BS to the time that it is successfully transferred to the UE for DL, or from a UE to a BS for UL. If the delay is larger than a given PDB for the packet, the packet is said to violate PDB, otherwise the packet is said to be successfully delivered.<br>- Values for PDB, e.g., {10ms, 20ms, 30ms, 50ms, 100ms, 200ms, 300ms, 1000ms, 2000ms} can be considered.<br>- Which values will be used will consider the use case for the evaluations. | [Chair notes RAN1#123 - eom3](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_123/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23123%20-%20eom3.docx)<br>`[123-R20-6GR-Evaluation]` |

| RAN1#123 | 11.2 | Agreement | For traffic model(s) for AI/ML services, the following can be considered:<br>- Packet size:<br>  - How to model the packet size, a fixed one or multiple values, or modelled as a random variable.<br>- Packet arrival:<br>  - FFS the details to determine the packet arrival rate, e.g.,<br>    - N multiple packets arrive together as a burst. The burst interval time is modelled as a random variable.<br>      - Within the burst, the N packets arrive according to a statistical distribution.<br>    - Packets arrive separately.<br>  - FFS whether/how to model the Jitter and the relation with the packet arrival.<br>- FFS: Whether the packet importance is known. Whether/how to reflect the packet importance.<br>- Whether/How to consider the PDB, e.g., Packet delay budget: The latency characteristic of the traffic in RAN side (i.e., air interface) is modelled as packet delay budget (PDB). The PDB is a limited time budget for a packet to be transmitted over the air from a base station to a UE, or from a UE to a base station<br>- FFS Whether/how to consider the Packet success rate requirement: [xx%] and the relation with the PDB.<br>- FFS how to model different cases, e.g., image-based GenAI, video-based GenAI, and chatbot, etc.<br>- FFS: Whether/how other traffic models (e.g., XR, FTP1/3) can be used to reflect above characteristics.<br>Note: input from SA4 if any will be considered. | [Chair notes RAN1#123 - eom3](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_123/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23123%20-%20eom3.docx)<br>`[123-R20-6GR-Evaluation]` |

| RAN1#123 | 11.1 | Agreement | - For scalable 6GR design for diverse device types, RAN1 can at least consider the following, targeting applicable to all 6G device types,<br>  - Basic initial access procedures from RAN1 perspective<br>  - Other PHY features after initial access procedure, e.g., Other DL/UL control, scheduling/HARQ<br>  - Coverage features to meet the identified coverage target<br>  - Energy saving both at BS and UE sides<br>  - MRSS<br>  - Note: whether these features are supported, mandatory or optional is separate discussion | [Chair notes RAN1#123 - eom3](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_123/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23123%20-%20eom3.docx)<br>`[123-R20-6GR-Overall]` |
| RAN1#123 | 11.1 | Agreement | - For the RAN1 study of “Re-use of existing 5G mid-band (~3.5GHz) site grid for 6G deployments in at least around 7 GHz and targeting comparable coverage to 5G mid-band”,<br>  - The link budget template candidates 1 and 2 are used to calculate the metric(s) as starting point to compare existing 5G mid-band and 6G deployments in at least around 7 GHz, with potential future update.<br>  - During initial access/random access<br>    - Coverage target is referring the bottleneck channel (i.e. Rel-15 NR Msg3) during initial access/random access for existing 5G mid-band<br>  - FFS target value(s) of data rate for data channels relative to 5G mid-band<br>  - Following deployment scenarios are considered<br>    - Urban macro (both O2I and outdoor)<br>    - Sub-urban macro (both O2I and outdoor)<br>  - Following carrier frequencies are considered to calculate the metric(s)<br>    - [4 GHz] as the existing 5G mid-band<br>    - 7 GHz as 6G deployment<br>  - Template in R1-2509615 is to be used for collecting inputs on the values from companies.<br>[Post-123-R20-6GR-Overall] – Shinya (DCM)<br>Email discussion for collecting inputs on the values from companies for link budget template, Jan 26th until 30th | [Chair notes RAN1#123 - eom3](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_123/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23123%20-%20eom3.docx)<br>`[123-R20-6GR-Overall]` |

| RAN1#122 | 11.3.2 | Agreement | - 6GR takes the following SCS as start point for discussion for all the signals/channels except PRACH.<br>  - For sub 6GHz<br>    - The following subcarrier spacing is at least supported<br>      - 15kHz SCS for FDD, 30kHz SCS for TDD<br>    - FFS: 30kHz SCS for FDD for around e.g., 1-2.5GHz<br>    - FFS: 7.5kHz SCS for sub1GHz (FDD)<br>    - Whether to discuss the FFS will be subject to RANP decision.<br>  - For around 7GHz<br>    - The following subcarrier spacing options can be studied<br>      - 30kHz, 60kHz<br>  - FFS: For around 15GHz<br>    - The following subcarrier spacing options can be studied<br>      - 30kHz, 60kHz, 120kHz<br>    - Whether to discuss it will be subject to RANP decision<br>  - For between 24.25GHz - 52.6GHz<br>    - Subcarrier spacing 120kHz is supported<br>  - FFS whether to allow using additional subcarrier spacing for SSB<br>- FFS subcarrier spacing for PRACH and up to initial access discussion. | [Chair notes RAN1#122 eom](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23122%20eom.zip)<br>`[122-R20-6GR-Frame structure]` |

| RAN1#122bis | 11.3.2 | Agreement | For communication, 6GR considers NR frame structure used as a starting point for the study item,<br>  - Resource defined by one subcarrier and one symbol is called as resource element (RE).<br>  - Resource block (RB) is defined where the number of consecutive subcarriers per RB is the same for all numerologies and the number of subcarriers per RB is 12<br>  - Radio Frame length is 10ms<br>  - Each radio frame is split into 10 subframes, each with a duration of 1 ms<br>  - For given SCS and for given symbol, the symbol duration, normal CP length and boundary is same as NR design.<br>  - A slot is defined as supporting 14 consecutive symbols for normal CP case and all subcarrier spacings. | [Chair notes RAN1#122b eom4](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_122b/Inbox/Chair_Notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23122b%20eom4.docx)<br>`[122bis-R20-6GR-Frame structure]` |

| RAN1#123 | 11.6 | Agreement | For study/evaluation of the performance and feasibility of AI/ML use cases in 6GR, at least the following may be considered<br>  - Intermediate performance KPIs (e.g., SGCS), link level KPIs (e.g., BLER) and system level KPIs (e.g., throughput vs overhead), etc<br>  - Computation complexity/latency (inference/monitoring)<br>  - Power consumption, if feasible to evaluate<br>  - Model size<br>  - Data collection impact<br>  - Scalability (refer to the examples in TR 38.843)<br>  - Generalization performance<br>    - FFS on whether and how to consider realistic deployment scenarios<br>  - Overhead/complexity associated with data collection, inferencing, performance monitoring, online/site specific fine-tuning, inter-vendor collaboration (if applicable)<br>  - Online training/fine-tuning training latency, if feasible to evaluate<br>  - Inter-vendor collaboration impact, if applicable<br>Note: Details to be discussed per use case.<br>Note: above aspects may be considered for both AI/ML and non-AI counter part | [Chair notes RAN1#123 - eom3](https://www.3gpp.org/ftp/tsg_ran/WG1_RL1/TSGR1_123/Inbox/Chair_notes/Chair%20notes%20RAN1%23123%20-%20eom3.docx)<br>`[123-R20-6GR-AI/ML]` |
